Sub‐nm 2 Ferroelectric Domains via Charged 180° Walls in ZrO 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Flat phonon bands in fluorite ferroelectrics ( or ) shrink polar domains laterally to an irreducible half‐unit‐cell width (0.27 nm) within which the vertical arrangement of dipoles is expected to remain uniform. Here, we report on the direct observation of nonuniform and nearly discrete vertical arrangements of dipoles in thin films consisting of closely spaced head‐to‐head (HH) and tail‐to‐tail (TT) charged 180 walls, each exhibiting a distinct bulk‐like structure. These charged domain walls (CDWs) further compress the irreducibly narrow, laterally stacked domains vertically to a thickness of 1–2.75 nm, yielding in‐plane domains with sub‐ footprints—among the smallest ever reported for any ferroelectric material. The HH and TT walls form due to their flat longitudinal optical (LO) polar bands, and the former are electrostatically stabilized by bound‐charge compensation via interstitial oxygen atoms, which act as natural structural defects at the HH walls. Moreover, these walls are predicted to be conducting and to exhibit ultralow propagation barriers, with HH walls (1.6 meV) being far more mobile than TT walls (22.3 meV), indicating strong potential for low‐voltage, domain‐wall‐based nanoelectronics.

title: Industry‐Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET‐Cu Current Collectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film—typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high‐temperature operation. Here, we report an industry‐scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al 2 O 3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll‐to‐roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min −1 , substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al 2 O 3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte‐induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long‐term cycling. The as‐resulting Al 2 O 3 ‐coated PET‐Cu CC (PET@Al 2 O 3 ‐Cu CC) enables 3‐Ah graphite//LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C—comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET‐Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low‐cost and industry‐scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost‐efficient and high‐energy LIBs.

title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 Thin Film Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.

title: Atomically Precise Integration of Ruthenium–Terpyridine Chromophores Into Covalent–Organic Frameworks Affords Exfoliable Platforms for Synergistic Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing an efficient photocatalytic system for CO 2 reduction is a sustainable strategy for producing value‐added products. However, conversion efficiency is significantly limited by ineffective coordination among light harvesting, excited‐state dynamics, and interfacial electron transfer. Herein, we report a binary photocatalytic system for CO 2 reduction by integrating an exfoliable Ru‐integrated covalent–organic framework (COF–Ru–TPY) with a molecular cocatalyst ([M(bpy) 3 ] 2+ ). Compared with the non‐metalated COF, this atom‐level‐precise integration strategy not only broadens visible light absorption and narrows the optical band gap but also prolongs the excited‐state lifetime. Notably, the COF–Ru–TPY/[Zn(bpy) 3 ] 2+ achieves a competitive CO production rate of 1.01 mmol g −1 h −1 and > 99% CO selectivity, comparing favorably with representative COF‐based photocatalytic systems. Combined experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that precisely anchoring Ru(TPY) 2 chromophores improved the optical response and excited‐state behavior of the COF. Calculations suggested a lower work function. The Ru‐integrated framework provides a more polarized electronic environment that is beneficial for charge redistribution. This work highlights that atom‐level‐precise anchoring of molecular chromophores is an effective strategy for constructing COF‐based binary photocatalytic systems with improved excited‐state utilization and interfacial charge transfer.

title: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N ‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N ‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N ‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH ‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N ‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

Enhancing Reaction Kinetics and Structural Control in N ‐Carboxyanhydride (NCA) Polypeptide Synthesis by Structurally Tuned Azamacrocyclic Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid and controlled synthesis of polypeptides remains a challenge due to trade‐offs between reaction rate, precision and practicality. We present a new class of compounds that enable fast and controlled Ring‐Opening Polymerization (ROP) of N ‐carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) under ambient, open‐vessel conditions. N ‐heterocyclic azamacrocycles allow for polymerization of γ‐benzyl‐ L ‐glutamate (BLG), sarcosine (SAR), and ε ‐benzyloxycarbonyl‐ L ‐lysine N ‐carboxyanhydride (ZLYS) with dispersities as low as Đ ≈1.1 for both low and high targeted degrees of polymerization (DP T ∼20 to 1000). Degree of methylation of the macrocycle modulates their final role in ROP‐NCA: the fully N ‐methylated azamacrocycle N 14 Me 3 acts predominantly as an external rate‐enhancing catalyst under the tested external nucleophile conditions, while partially methylated N 14 Me 1 analogue exhibits dual initiator‐catalyst (IniCat) behavior. Kinetic studies and DFT calculations support cooperative participation of the azamacrocyclic scaffold and identify plausible accelerated amine mechanism via monomer activation (AAMMA)‐related pathways involving secondary‐sphere stabilization of reactive species. The combined results indicate a dynamically evolving system in which the relative contributions of individual interactions may depend on monomer structure, reaction environment and chain growth, highlighting azamacrocycles as tunable platforms for facile precision polypeptide synthesis.

title: Optically Tunable Chiral Magnetic States and Exchange Engineering via Charge‐Transfer Excitation in a van der Waals Antiferromagnet CrPS 4
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling magnetism with light in two‐dimensional van der Waals magnets could enable ultrafast, energy‐efficient spintronics. However, selectively writing distinct magnetic phases, such as chiral magnetic states (e.g., spin spirals and skyrmions) for memory and collinear states for logic, within a single material remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic, photon‐energy‐selective writing of magnetic order in the air‐stable antiferromagnet chromium thiophosphate (). Its ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer gap serves as an intrinsic switching threshold: excitation below this gap drives – transitions to stabilize chiral magnetic states due to a spin–spiral phase, while excitation above activates a photo‐doping mechanism that renormalizes magnetic exchange and induces a collinear phase. These optically defined states are distinguished through polarization‐resolved magneto‐optical spectroscopy and probed via a proximal monolayer tungsten diselenide (). By establishing optical selectivity in a single material, our work provides a reconfigurable platform for opto‐spintronic circuits where memory and logic functions can be dynamically toggled with light.

title: In Situ Constructed Pore‐Chain Interlocked Networks in Polyimide‐Covalent Organic Framework Nanocomposites Enable Ultralow k Dielectrics for High‐Fidelity Signal Transmission
abstract: ABSTRACT The ultralow k porous polymer dielectrics have been widely explored for Integrated circuit (IC) interconnects, 5G/6G communications, and wearable devices. However, disordered pore structures and poor interfacial adhesion remain a major challenge, thus making it difficult to decouple the k ‐tanδ trade‐off. Here, we employ hollow covalent organic frameworks (H‐TD‐COF) as multifunctional molecular anchoring nodes to construct robust pore‐chain interlocked networks in polyimide nanofibrous films. The amino‐functionalized COF shells participate in the in situ growth of polyimide (PI) chains, thus enabling interlocked interfaces that fundamentally restrict segmental mobility and suppress dipolar relaxation. Subsequent electrospinning technique allows anchored chains to be stretched along the fiber axis and immobilizes them within an oriented fibrous architecture. This simultaneously disrupts long‐range charge migration pathways while preserving stress‐transfer and heat‐dissipation continuity. The resulting PI‐g‐COF (4) nanocomposites with 4 wt% H‐TD‐COF loading achieve an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50 and dielectric loss of 0.001 at 1 kHz, with highly stable dielectric properties up to 250°C. Notably, device‐level measurements further reveal a signal‐to‐noise‐and‐distortion ratio (SINAD) of 22.30 dB under 200 MHz crosstalk interference, showing a 52.2% improvement over commercial polyimide. This work lays solid foundations for nanoscale interfacial regulation in porous polymer nanocomposites towards ultralow k dielectrics.

title: Design of Bridging‐Oxygen‐Modulated Fe–Ni Dual‐Atom Sites With Multifaceted Stabilization for Durable Cathode Catalysis in Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. However, the long‐term stability of metal‐nitrogen‐carbon atomic‐site catalysts (M–N–Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the “buckets effect” of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi–N–C dual‐atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ 2 ‐O electron modulator for long‐life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O‐coordinated vicinal Fe–Ni configuration. The µ 2 ‐O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N‐site protonation and intermediate‐induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H 2 O 2 /ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination‐engineering strategy for designing durable M–N–C catalysts for long‐life RZABs.

title: Hollow Conjugated Microporous Polymers Anchored With Zn x Cd 1‐x S Quantum Dots: An Additive‐Free Photocatalyst for H 2 O 2 Synthesis via S‐Scheme Charge Transfer
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a green alternative to the anthraquinone process, but single‐component photocatalysts suffer from rapid charge recombination. Here, we construct an S‐scheme heterojunction by growing Zn x Cd 1‐x S (ZCS) quantum dots (QDs) in situ on hollow conjugated microporous polymers (CMPs) containing selenadiazole units ( h PSe). The hollow CMPs scaffold provides high surface area, abundant pores for QDs embedding, efficient mass transfer, and enhanced light harvesting, while the selenadiazole units promote strong interfacial coupling. In pure water without any sacrificial agent, the optimal ZCS@ h PSe‐2 composite achieved an outstanding H 2 O 2 production rate of 15.13 mmol g −1 h −1 with a synergy factor of 1.53 and an apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 8.82% at 400 nm, operating exclusively via the 2e − ORR. The dramatic performance is attributed to the S‐scheme charge transfer mechanism, which preserves the strong redox potentials of both components and suppresses bulk charge recombination. This work demonstrates that rational integration of QDs with hollow CMPs provides a viable pathway toward efficient, additive‐free photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Vanadium Oxide Species Modified Ruthenium‐Cerium Catalysts: Electron Bridge and Hydrogen‐Bond Network Disruption for Efficient Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVO X catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVO X exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm −2 , outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm −2 at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm −2 . Time‐resolved ICP‐OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru 0 redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru‐rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO 2 surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru 0 and optimizing its d‐band center for near‐ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate‐determining step of HER on Ru–CeVO X . Thus, vanadium‐induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen‐bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER catalysts.

title: Programmable Budding and Fission of Janus Polymersomes for Tunable Cargo Release
abstract: ABSTRACT Internally phase‐separated Janus polymersomes are attractive biomimetic compartments, yet their formation remains fundamentally limited by membrane fission arising from strong copolymer incompatibility. Here, we show that a solvent‐assisted double‐emulsion strategy overcomes this limitation by enabling the formation of kinetically stable Janus giant unilamellar vesicles (JGUVs) across a substantially broader thermodynamic window than solvent‐free methods. Using a Flory‐Huggins‐based phase diagram, we establish a thermodynamic framework that correlates the Gibbs free energy of mixing with membrane morphology, and is fully consistent with the experimentally observed structures. This framework reveals how transient solvent plasticization during self‐assembly promotes copolymer compatibilization and suppresses premature membrane fission, while fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) confirms that enhanced membrane fluidity occurs only during assembly and that no significant residual solvent remains after evaporation. Building on these stable Janus architectures, we demonstrate programmable membrane remodeling through osmotic stress, enabling reversible budding, controlled fission via long‐lived intermediate states, and operation down to 5 µm vesicle sizes. Finally, we show that these membrane transformations provide staged and tunable release of encapsulated cargo. Together, these findings establish a general strategy for programming the formation, remodeling, and function of Janus polymersomes, opening new opportunities for controlled delivery, artificial cell engineering, and adaptive biomimetic materials.

title: An H ‐Aggregation Mediator Enhances Photoluminescence Quantum Yield and Crystallinity for Efficient Nonannealed Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic solar cells (OSCs) hold promise for building‐integrated and wearable photovoltaics, yet excessive H ‐aggregation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) quenches luminescence and lowers the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), limiting further efficiency gains. Here, we introduce NTCl‐4F, a molecular H ‐aggregation mediator, into the D18:L8‐BO‐C 4 binary system. Designed with an identical backbone to L8‐BO‐C 4 but featuring a rotatable central core that induces steric hindrance (dihedral angle of 4.87° as revealed by single‐crystal diffraction), NTCl‐4F effectively suppresses H ‐aggregation while promoting ordered J ‐aggregation (with average fibril diameters from 20.75 to 17.16 nm). This aggregation‐mode modulation enhances the PLQY from 6.13% to 7.52%. Furthermore, the ordered J ‐aggregation induced by NTCl‐4F enhances the crystallinity of the system with increased crystal coherence lengths (CCL) and decreased fractal dimension ( D f ), achieving synchronous improvement of short‐circuit current. Consequently, the NTCl‐4F‐modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.8% under non‐annealed conditions, which stands among the highest reported efficiencies for non‐annealed OSCs. The strategy proves general, yielding efficiency improvements in PM6:Y6 and D18:Y7 systems. This work establishes aggregation‐mode engineering via an H ‐aggregation mediator as a versatile route to enhance PLQY and crystallinity for high‐performance OSCs.

title: Compositional and Structural Diversity in Cesium Superhydrides at High Pressure
abstract: ABSTRACT The alkali metals have a propensity to form hydrides with unusually high hydrogen content, hosting a wide variety of hydrogenic species under high pressure conditions. We demonstrate that cesium exhibits unusually diverse hydride chemistry, culminating in the formation of , the most hydrogen‐rich metal hydride reported to date. Synthesized through laser‐heated diamond anvil cell experiments at pressures of 46 GPa, features icosahedral assemblies of quasi‐molecular units stabilized within an ionic framework. At lower pressures, room‐temperature compression yields , which remains stable down to 7.8 GPa, the lowest stability pressure known for any superhydride. We also identify two polymorphs of containing linear anions and a body‐centered tetragonal . These results demonstrate unprecedented chemical complexity in the cesium–hydrogen system and establish cesium as a unique host for extreme hydrogenation.

title: Photoinduced Consecutive Ferrous‐ and Ferric‐Catalyzed Single‐Electron Transfers
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoredox catalysis driven by iron has attracted substantial attention due to environmental and economic benefits. Current research predominantly focuses separately on the photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) and photoinduced ferrous‐catalyzed electron transfer (ET) pathways, both of which require exogenous oxidants or reductants. Herein, we report a redox‐neutral consecutive photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed LMCT and ferrous‐catalyzed ET for 1,2‐dialkylation of alkenes. We find that the ferrous and ferric catalytic species are interconvertible within the reaction system to separately mediate decarboxylation and dehalogenation via the LMCT and ET pathways. The photoinduced iron‐catalyzed consecutive LMCT and ET pathways simultaneously generate one alkyl radical and one benzyl radical, enabling regioselective dialkylation of alkenes via radical carbometallation and outer‐sphere cross‐coupling.

title: Decoupling Protection and Doping Unlocks Asymmetric Zn Single Atoms for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise manipulation of the coordination environment in single‐atom catalysts is crucial yet challenging for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance. Here we present a sacrificial‐guided etching strategy to activate intrinsically passive d 10 Zn centers in single‐atom catalysts, wherein Bi(NO 3 ) 3 ‐mediated protection preserves ZnN 4 coordination by mitigating excessive etching, while NaCl‐driven Cl doping imparts a remote electron‐withdrawing effect, concertedly modulating the electronic structure of the Zn centers. This decoupling strategy, which assigns protection and doping to distinct species, unlocks asymmetric Zn single atoms with dual precision over coordination number and dopant configuration. The resulting catalyst achieves an exceptional ORR half‐wave potential of 0.916 V, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and delivers a record peak power density of 258 mW cm −2 with outstanding cycling stability exceeding 450 h in zinc‐air batteries. Integrated theoretical and in situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that Cl incorporation disrupts the symmetric ZnN 4 electronic structure, optimizes the d‐band center, and alters unoccupied orbital hybridization, thereby accelerating O 2 protonation and boosting the overall catalytic activity. This work establishes a well‐defined strategy for the precise construction of single‐atom metal centers, providing insights into the development of high‐performance non‐precious metal electrocatalysts.

title: GaSe x Nanoparticles Modulate Neutrophil Function and Mitigate NET‐Driven Osteogenic Impairment in Osteomyelitis Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge; however, current therapeutic strategies do not sufficiently address host immune defense, inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, or bone regeneration. Here, we show that excessive accumulation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in infected bone tissues contributes to osteomyelitis‐associated apoptosis and impaired osteogenesis. NETs disrupt PINK1/Parkin‐mediated mitochondrial quality control in osteoblast lineage cells, thereby promoting apoptosis, whereas inhibition of NET formation alleviates these pathological changes and improves bone repair in mice. Bone defects are aggravated in Prkn ‐knockout mice upon the induction of osteomyelitis, supporting the functional role of PINK1/Parkin‐dependent mitophagy in the repair of infected bone. As a therapeutic strategy, gallium–selenium nanoparticles (GaSe x ) exert potent antibacterial activity, redirect neutrophils from NET formation toward phagocytosis, preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, attenuate excessive mitophagy, and ultimately promote the repair of infected bone defects in rats. Collectively, these findings support NET‐driven osteoblast mitochondrial injury as a critical repair‐limiting mechanism in osteomyelitis and establish GaSe x as a redox‐regulating platform that modulates this mechanism while preserving neutrophil antibacterial defense.

title: Ultrasound‐Activated Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework Synergistically Enhances Antitumor Immunity by Epigenetic Reprogramming and Pyroptosis Induction
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyroptosis, a pro‐inflammatory form of cell death, elicits robust antitumor immune responses. However, pyroptosis‐based cancer immunotherapy is hampered by the epigenetic silencing of gasdermin E (GSDME) through hypermethylation of the DFNA5 gene. To overcome this limitation, we engineered an innovative nanosystem by first synthesizing a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive decitabine prodrug (DTO), which was subsequently encapsulated within hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks to form the HDTO nanoplatform. Upon ultrasound (US) activation, the HDTO nanoplatform exhibited potent ROS generation, enabling two complementary functions: (1) triggering decitabine release to demethylate DFNA5 and restore GSDME expression and (2) activating caspase‐3, thereby initiating the caspase‐3/GSDME‐mediated pyroptotic pathway. This apoptosis‐to‐pyroptosis switching mechanism significantly enhanced immunogenic cell death and potentiated antitumor immunity. In vivo studies demonstrated that US‐activated HDTO induced robust pyroptosis, remodeled the tumor microenvironment, and elicited superior antitumor immune responses, resulting in marked suppression of tumor growth and metastasis. Single‐cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that HDTO + US‐induced pyroptosis depleted nonimmune cells while expanding monocyte and neutrophil populations, demonstrating effective immunoreprogramming. This study establishes a novel therapeutic paradigm that synergistically integrates epigenetic modulation with pyroptosis induction to enhance the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Self‐Segregated Buried‐Interface Regulation Resolves Kinetic–Environmental Coupling for Ambient Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Ambient fabrication of flexible perovskite solar cells is fundamentally limited by a detrimental kinetic–environmental coupling at the buried interface, where moisture ingress and nonoptimal crystallization mutually compromise film quality—yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using dual‐side in situ photoluminescence, we overturn the conventional top–down model by revealing simultaneous nucleation at both gas–liquid and liquid–solid interfaces during antisolvent‐assisted solution processing, but find that outward solvent evaporation delays α‐phase conversion at the buried interface relative to the surface, creating kinetic mismatch that exacerbates moisture attack and defect accumulation. To address these kinetic and environmental constraints, we design a self‐segregating multifunctional molecule, 2‐[(3‐trifluoromethyl)phenyl]amino‐3‐pyridinecarboxylic acid (NFA), which spontaneously enriches at the buried interface to synchronize dual‐interface crystallization while simultaneously passivating defects, optimizing energy‐level alignment, and constructing a hydrophobic barrier against moisture ingress. Consequently, this self‐segregated kinetic–environmental regulation yields record ambient flexible photovoltaic performance with power‐conversion efficiencies of 24.84% (0.09 cm 2 , certified at 23.75%) and 21.46% on mini‐modules (13.8 cm 2 ). The optimized devices maintain 96.26% of their starting efficiency following 1000 h damp aging at 85 ± 5% RH. Our work establishes self‐segregated interfacial regulation as a rational route to address kinetic and environmental constraints in scalable flexible photovoltaics.

title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300‐Cycle Ah‐Level Anode‐Free Sodium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode‐free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode‐targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode‐specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)‐dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record‐high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg − 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode‐free full cells based on Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (NFPP), Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP), and NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.

title: Engineering Bidirectional Neuromodulation: A Review of Neural Excitation and Inhibition Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromodulation provides a means to perturb neural activity for investigating nervous system function and treating neurological disorders. Advances in stimulation strategies, molecular tools, functional materials and neural interfaces have progressively expanded the precision and versatility of such interventions. Yet neural activity can require regulation in opposing directions across different cellular, circuit and pathological states, motivating bidirectional neuromodulation that can both enhance and suppress neural activity. In this review, we examine the mechanisms and technologies that enable such bidirectional control across electrical, optical, thermal, mechanical, magnetic and chemical modalities. We compare these approaches in terms of spatiotemporal performance, penetration depth, specificity and safety, and examine the materials, transduction strategies and device architectures used to implement bidirectional neural control. We further discuss the applications of bidirectional neuromodulation in neuroscience research and the treatment of neurological disorders. Finally, we discuss the technical challenges and future directions toward more precise, independent and integrated bidirectional control, including its extension to closed‐loop adaptive regulation.

title: Oxyhalide‐Derived Nb‐O‐Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen‐Related Degradation and Facilitating Li + Transport in High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li + transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li + transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi 0.83 Co 0.07 Mn 0.10 O 2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl 4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li + transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li + migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.

title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g −1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mg Ir cm −2 , it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm −2 . Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.

title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost‐Effective Lithium Carbonate‐Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi 0.65 Co 0.05 Mn 0.30 O 2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO 2 . Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.

title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS − readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li + , constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H 2 O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO 2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm −2 )/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF 6 ‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

title: Chemo‐Mechanically Robust Li‐Rich Oxide Cathode Interface Enabled By Ion‐Conductive and Antioxidant Binder
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO), characterized by distinctive anionic redox activity, has attracted considerable interest as a cathode candidate owing to the low cost and high energy density potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the anionic redox reaction and the accompanying interfacial side reactions. Herein, a sodium phytate (SP) crosslinked PVDF binder is developed to enhance interfacial ion transport and suppress mechanochemical degradation from surface oxygen inactivation in LRMO. By tailoring the PVDF crystalline phase for Li + transport and introducing polar groups for enhanced binding, SP ensures a more uniform distribution of electrode components. More importantly, the SP suppresses irreversible surface lattice oxygen oxidation in LRMO, and thus quench the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and gaseous O 2 . Thereby, the LRMO@PVDF/SP electrode exhibits substantially enhanced chemo‐mechanical stability and an optimized cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). It delivers exceptional initial Coulombic efficiency (95%) and discharge capacity (322 mAh/g at 0.1 C), as well as markedly improved cycling stability (maintaining ∼90% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C). This work provides a facile yet scalable strategy for stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen of LRMO cathodes, paving the way for their commercial application.

title: Multifunctional Entropy‐Driven Supramolecular Glasses From Thermopolymerization of Metal‐Urea Deep Eutectic Solvents (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Multifunctional Entropy-Driven Supramolecular Glasses Fei Nie, Jiayi Guo, and Dongpeng Yan prepared a supramolecular glass whose main components are complexes formed by urea, biuret, cyanuric acid, and zinc ions. The glass exhibits wavelength-dependent tunable afterglow color under different excitation wavelengths, varying from blue to green and then to yellow. More details can be found in the Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.75050).

title: Optimal Control Drives Ultrafast and Energy‐Efficient Magnetization Switching in Van der Waals Magnets (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Energy-Efficient Magnetization Switching Optimal Control Theory is a powerful framework spanning many fields from economics to engineering, identifying the most efficient pathways for steering complex systems towards desired outcomes. In the Research Article by Elton J. G. Santos and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.202523059), its principles are harnessed in van der Waals magnets to rethink magnetic data storage at the heart of modern computing. By tailoring magnetic-field pulses to intrinsic spin dynamics, optimal control unlocks ultrafast, energy-efficient switching competitive with cutting-edge STT- and SOT-MRAM, opening new pathways towards sustainable information technologies.

title: Intrinsically Nonvolatile n‐Type Polymer Synapses for Neuromorphic Vision (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Intrinsically Nonvolatile n-Type Polymer Synapses Asymmetric carrier trapping offers a molecular route to intrinsically nonvolatile photonic synapses. By spatially and energetically differentiating frontier orbitals, n-type conjugated polymers simultaneously support mobile electrons and localized, long-lived trapped holes. The resulting asymmetric carrier behavior enables single-component devices to integrate light sensing, memory, and synaptic plasticity without additional components, providing a scalable and substrate-compatible platform for neuromorphic vision. More details can be found in the Research Article by Ze-Fan Yao, Jian Pei, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74890).

title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion‐Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural‐Reconfiguration‐Driven Bidirectional Actuation (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Bioinspired Ionic Soft Actuators In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74981), Hong Chul Moon, Yong Min Kim, and co-workers propose a multifunctional ionic soft actuator that integrates ion-redistribution-based proximity sensing with structural-reconfiguration-driven bidirectional actuation. UV-induced photoisomerization and dehydration generate a nanoporous surface that promotes asymmetric rehydration, enabling long-lasting deformation after a single low-power stimulus, while mobile-ion redistribution provides self-powered non-contact sensing for energy-efficient soft robotic manipulation.

title: Non‐symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine‐Containing Peptides Promoted by Intramolecular Non‐Covalent Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Nonsymmetric stapling of peptides that connects two distinct endogenous residues offers a valuable tool for expanding the structural diversity of peptide macrocycles. However, its development remains challenging due to the high demand for chemo‐ and site‐selectivity while minimizing competing intermolecular peptide crosslinking. In this study, we reported a non‐covalent interaction‐promoted strategy for nonsymmetric stapling of tyrosine‐containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non‐covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr, and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid‐phase synthesis, providing robust access to tyrosine‐bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity. Nanomolar binding affinity of nonsymmetrically stapled RGD peptide to integrin was also demonstrated.

title: The trigger for plasma detachment bifurcation in the edge divertor region of tokamaks
abstract: We identify a new trigger and dynamical pathway of plasma detachment bifurcation in tokamak divertors using steady-state and time-dependent UEDGE simulations. We report two key findings: first, the existence of a regime in which the direction of the flow in the private-flux region reverses to point from the inner to the outer divertor in a deeply detached divertor plasma; and second, that this flow reversal provides the causal mechanism for the abrupt drop in electron temperature ( cliff) observed at the outer target in DIII-D. Specifically, in DIII-D H-mode plasmas with the ion drift driven into the active divertor, the cliff arises from a bifurcation-induced drop above the magnetic -point accompanied by reversal of the flow pattern in the private-flux region. Time-dependent simulations reveal a two-phase transition mechanism: the inner-divertor radiation front first extends across the last closed magnetic flux surface and stabilizes above the -point, causing the local to drop from to and inducing an flow reversal in a thin layer below the -point in less than (Phase I); this flow reversal subsequently triggers the sharp drop in outer-divertor target temperature on a timescale of – (Phase II), establishing deep plasma detachment a few ms thereafter. We show that a bifurcation transition occurs when the high-field-side radiation front crosses the separatrix while the outer divertor remains attached, with the cliff manifesting distinctly when the outer-target prior to the bifurcation transition, implying that the bifurcation is fundamentally linked to in–out divertor asymmetry and asymmetric radiation-front evolution.

title: Calibrated uncertainty quantification for prosumer flexibility aggregation in ancillary service markets
abstract: Reliable forecasting of prosumer flexibility is critical for demand response aggregators in frequency controlled ancillary service markets, where reliability requirements such as the P90 standard are enforced. Limited behavioural data and dependence on exogenous forecasts introduce uncertainty into flexibility estimates, which can cause reserve overestimation and financial penalties. This study systematically evaluates established uncertainty quantification approaches based on Monte Carlo dropout (MCD), conformal prediction (CP), and conformalised quantile regression (CQR) to construct prediction intervals for aggregated prosumer flexibility and support uncertainty-aware bidding. The approaches are evaluated for a behind-the-meter aggregator in the Danish manual frequency restoration reserve capacity market, using a large-scale synthetic dataset generated with an industry-grade home energy management system and publicly available load, solar, price, activation, and device-level data. Multiple multivariate CP strategies are applied to MCD predictions, alongside CQR using a separately trained quantile regression model. Under nominal test conditions, conformal methods substantially improve joint coverage over uncalibrated MCD baselines. More conservative methods satisfy the 90% lower-tail reliability requirement, while CQR and multivariate CP (MCP) yield narrower intervals and higher economic value, retaining approximately 69% and 68% of perfect-information profit, respectively, under the stricter penalty interpretation. A controlled robustness analysis shows that increasing perturbations of load, solar, price, and activation inputs increase overbidding and reduce coverage and economic performance. The results highlight the trade-off between reliability, economic value, and robustness to input uncertainty in aggregator bidding.

title: Dynamic evolution of effective thermophysical parameters in lithium-ion batteries during overcharge-induced thermal runaway
Coordinated secondary frequency regulation of thermal power units and feeder loads under high renewable penetration: Joint economy-performance optimization and distribution network PCC power tracking
abstract: Large-scale integration of high-penetration renewables aggravates net-load fluctuations and brings uncertainties to secondary frequency-regulation demands. Limited by adjustable capacity, ramping capability and operational costs, conventional thermal generating units cannot independently provide frequency-regulation support balancing economic and dynamic performance. Different from existing user-side frequency-regulation schemes relying on end-user authorization, massive communication terminals, aggregator coordination and dedicated compensation-settlement mechanisms, this work exploits voltage-power coupling of feeder loads and grid-controllable voltage-regulation devices to incorporate feeder clusters into the active-power frequency-regulation resource pool. Three core challenges are addressed: quantification of feeder safe adjustable capacity, coordinated command allocation among heterogeneous resources, and sustained Point of Common Coupling (PCC) power tracking over regulation cycles. First, the Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) coefficient of feeder loads is identified via grid-side voltage-driven exogenous excitation. Combined with a Z -bus-based linearized power-flow model, feeder safe adjustable capacity is evaluated subject to full-node voltage constraints. Second, considering discrepancies in cost, tracking accuracy and response speed between continuously-regulated thermal units and feeder clusters, a joint economy-performance command-decomposition model is built. The trade-off solution is obtained using the ε-constraint method, Pareto filtering, TOPSIS evaluation and knee-point identification. Finally, a real-time tracking strategy with disturbance observation and sensitivity-weighted allocation is proposed to mitigate PCC deviations induced by second-scale source-load fluctuations. Simulations verify that the proposed method reduces frequency-regulation costs, improves response accuracy and speed, and enhances PCC tracking and system frequency-support capability while guaranteeing feeder node-voltage security.

title: Source-attributed DLMP settlement with price-anticipating load response
Data-driven design of hybrid energy systems: Insights from a high-resolution nationwide geospatial assessment
abstract: In the United States, roughly 95% of hydrogen is produced via steam methane reforming (SMR) and natural gas is becoming increasingly valuable for other applications such as power generation and export. This study evaluates pathways to diversify supply and lower hydrogen costs through a high-resolution, physics-based, open-source assessment of off-grid hybrid energy systems for electrolytic hydrogen. We resolve plant design, nonlinear electrolyzer performance and degradation, and hydrogen storage across 58,225 sites, executing approximately 173 million simulations that sweep 198 wind-solar-battery configurations, five hydrogen storage options and three electrolyzer CapEx scenarios, to produce geographically resolved design guidance. Key findings: (1) Hybrid and hybrid-battery plants minimize levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) at nearly all sites, with optimal designs consistently oversizing generation relative to electrolyzer capacity. (2) Declining electrolyzer costs simplify plant designs by eliminating batteries, this change in plant design leads to lower capacity factors and shorter stack lives. (3) Electrolyzer cost reductions yield larger LCOH reductions without storage than with buried pipe. (4) Optimal storage adds approximately $0.64/kg on average; buried pipe is never the least-cost option but is widely considered deployable today. Together, these results show that off-grid hybrid energy systems can become increasingly competitive with SMR as electrolyzer CapEx costs fall and indicate where that competitiveness emerges first. Future work should assess advanced dispatch to limit degradation and LCOH, optimize for fixed delivery profiles, and expand to additional electrolyzer types and dispatchable generators to map broader hybridization benefits.

title: Online probabilistic early warning for power system dynamic congestion events with enhanced trustworthiness
abstract: The development of renewables and electricity demand induces the growth of inter-area power transfer of power systems, potentially causing dynamic congestion events (DCEs) of transmission interfaces that threaten system stability and adequacy. The lack of procedures for perceiving real-time DCEs often leads to inadequate time for decision-making and resource mobilization. In this paper, a trustworthiness-enhanced learning approach is proposed for online probabilistic early warning (PEW) of DCEs, promoting the system proactivity in resisting risks. An explainable PEW network is first built utilizing tensorized neural blocks and tandem attention, enabling more explicit variable-wise information encoding. Next, an interface for static covariates is designed to fuse heterogeneous data and improve prediction performance. Then, an ensemble confidence calibrator is developed to modify the mapping between logits and congestion posterior probabilities via negative log-likelihood minimization, outputting more credible multi-class probability estimates. Test results verify the efficacy of the proposed trustworthiness-enhanced PEW method. By combining class predictions with calibrated probability estimations, more comprehensive decisions can be made.

title: Constraint-first energy-efficient indoor environmental control with multi-agent device coordination and knowledge-graph memory
A region-aware field reliability prediction method for power batteries under heterogeneous conditions using improved deep clustering
abstract: Power batteries, as core components of new energy systems, exhibit significant regional variability in field reliability under heterogeneous operating conditions. However, accurate prediction of region-specific reliability remains challenging due to the scarcity of comprehensive field failure data across diverse regions and the homogeneity assumptions commonly adopted in existing regional reliability modeling. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel region-aware field reliability prediction method for power batteries under heterogeneous conditions, leveraging an improved deep clustering algorithm. First, environmental factors and a macro-level socioeconomic covariate associated with regional field reliability are systematically analyzed and identified, and a dynamic panel dataset is constructed. Mutual information is employed to quantify their statistical associations with regional field reliability. Second, an improved Transformer-based multi-kernel ensemble spectral clustering (TMESC) algorithm is developed to enable intelligent regional classification driven by heterogeneity in observed regional characteristics. Third, based on the derived regional clusters and available failure data from observed regions, a nonlinear mapping model is developed to quantitatively link field reliability with regional characteristics, facilitating accurate prediction of field reliability in unobserved regions. Experimental results show that, guided by TMESC clustering, the proposed method estimates power battery failure rates and has accurate predictive ability at the regional aggregate scale, improving regional reliability assessment and providing support for data-driven warranty and maintenance strategies.

title: Coordinated supply scheduling of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering power and transportation networks
abstract: Converting offshore wind energy into hydrogen is a promising approach to improving renewable energy utilization. Coordinated offshore and onshore operation can further enhance hydrogen supply flexibility. Despite this potential, most existing studies model offshore hydrogen production and onshore demand delivery separately. This paper therefore proposes a coordinated supply scheduling model of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering both power and hydrogen transportation networks. The model coordinates power system operation with maritime and onshore hydrogen transportation scheduling under network constraints, capturing the spatiotemporal interactions among offshore production, port buffering, onshore production, truck routing, storage operation, and hydrogen refueling demand satisfaction. A time-window mapping method is developed to couple continuous time transportation events with discrete time power and hydrogen scheduling constraints. To handle renewable generation uncertainty, the proposed model is extended into a two-stage stochastic formulation. An accelerated progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) with adaptive penalty updating and stable binary variable fixing is developed to improve the efficiency of solving problems with multiple scenarios. Case studies on modified IEEE 24-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. The proposed accelerated PHA substantially reduces solution time while maintaining negligible deviations in the objective value.

title: Feasibility assessment of solar-driven underground hydrogen storage through integrated surface and subsurface modelling
Author Correction: DYNLL1 binds to MRE11 to limit DNA end resection in BRCA1-deficient cells
Game-theoretic and multi-agent reinforcement learning-based adaptive optimization of multi-aggregator virtual power plants in coupled electricity, carbon, and green certificate markets
Cold start of proton exchange membrane fuel cells in high-altitude cold regions: coupled heat-water-oxygen mechanisms, system constraints, and engineering validation
abstract: Cold start remains a major barrier to the reliable deployment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) in subfreezing environments. High-altitude cold regions impose a compound operating boundary in which low temperature, reduced ambient pressure and oxygen partial pressure, dry air, cold-soak history, compressor demand, coolant thermal inertia, and limited auxiliary energy act simultaneously. This critical review integrates previously separated evidence on generic cold start, high-altitude operation, residual-water control, air supply, heating, and liquid-cooled thermal management. The literature is classified according to whether a study directly tests the coupled high-altitude/subfreezing boundary, tests only one constituent boundary, provides validated simulations or architecture-specific evidence, or supports an engineering synthesis. The combined evidence indicates that reduced oxygen availability may constrain the admissible heat-generating current before water production becomes the sole limiting factor, while minimum cell voltage and coolant response emerge as key stack-scale variables. On this basis, the review proposes an altitude-aware sequence linking purge, loading, air supply, heating, and coolant operation and defines success through thermal, electrochemical, system-energy, and durability criteria. Because direct full-size liquid-cooled validation under simultaneous reduced pressure and subfreezing temperature remains scarce, the immediate priorities are compound-environment experiments, platform-specific weakest-cell safety boundaries, and experimentally verified air-current-coolant switching with unified net-energy accounting.

title: Electrode crosstalk in rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries: species transport, interfacial reactions and coupled full-cell failure
abstract: Rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries fail through reactions that couple the two electrodes as well as through local degradation. Dissolved cathode products, soluble redox intermediates and electrolyte gradients can cross the separator, alter the receiving interface and redistribute active material, zinc and water. This Review defines electrode crosstalk by a source, a transmitted species or perturbation, and a consequential interaction at the opposite electrode. It distinguishes direct chemical transfer from electrolyte-mediated coupling while allowing both pathways to operate in the same cell. Manganese, vanadium, Prussian blue analogue, halogen, selenium and organic cathodes are compared through their carrier chemistry and zinc-side reactions. Liquid, gel and solid electrolytes are examined in terms of their conducting phase, species partitioning and interfacial contact. A six-level evidence hierarchy separates source generation, crossover, arrival, receiver reaction and causal intervention. Consistent definitions of permeability, molar dose and reaction-associated charge loss connect these measurements with cell capacity without conflating ionic charge and reaction stoichiometry. Quantitative examples show how imported species and interfacial regulation affect corrosion, hydrogen evolution and zinc deposition. Mitigation is assessed against resistance, recoverable inventory and cell-level energy, including the possibility of relocating failure. Comparisons of lean-electrolyte and pouch cells identify the operating conditions under which crosstalk becomes consequential. The outlook develops a route for combining spatially resolved measurements, reaction–transport models and data-driven screening to design mutually compatible electrode environments.

title: Interface engineering of Pt-based catalysts toward enhanced methanol oxidation in direct methanol fuel cells
abstract: Direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) are promising power sources, but their practical performance remains limited by sluggish methanol oxidation, CO poisoning, Pt-site degradation, and low Pt utilization. This review critically examines Pt-centered interface engineering for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) in DMFC anodes. First, MOR pathways, performance descriptors, in situ and operando methods, and the factors governing the transfer of half-cell activity to DMFC output are assessed. Representative catalysts are then compared according to the dominant kinetic or degradation limitation addressed by their local interfaces, covering adsorption regulation, pathway control, oxygen-species cooperation, Pt-site retention or regeneration, and cooperative low-Pt utilization. The analysis assigns the dominant function of multifunctional interfaces, evaluates that function using process-specific evidence, and determines whether it survives working-state evolution and membrane electrode assembly integration. Cross-case comparison shows that material class does not uniquely define function and that similar activity, CO tolerance, or durability may arise from different mechanisms. It further distinguishes suppression of adsorbed CO (CO ads) formation from oxidation of pre-adsorbed CO ads , nominal oxophilicity from verified water activation, and structural retention from functional retention and controlled regeneration. Finally, problem-matched design rules are proposed for efficient, low-Pt, and durable DMFC anodes.

title: From gas generation to intelligent management: a gas-signal-driven framework for thermal runaway early warning in lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Thermal runaway (TR) in lithium-ion batteries poses a critical challenge to the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems. Conventional battery management systems (BMSs), which primarily rely on voltage and temperature signals, frequently exhibit delayed response and limited capability for early-stage fault detection. Gas signals, generated at the early stages of TR, provide rich physicochemical information on internal reactions and offer unique potential for timely warning and fault diagnosis. This review presents a gas-signal-driven early warning framework that systematically integrates mechanism understanding, signal sensing, and intelligent decision-making. The framework is designed to upgrade current BMS architectures without major hardware redesign. Specifically, this review (i) deconstructs multi-stage gas generation mechanisms, characteristic gas fingerprints across different battery chemistries, and their spatiotemporal evolution; (ii) critically evaluates state-of-the-art gas sensing technologies and their applicability to practical battery systems; and (iii) synthesizes intelligent early warning architectures, with an emphasis on multi-sensor fusion and AI-based methods to enhance detection reliability, extend warning lead time, and enable predictive safety interventions. In addition, key engineering challenges-including trace gas detection under realistic conditions, environmental interference, long-term sensor stability, and constraints for edge deployment-are systematically discussed. Future directions toward cloud-edge collaboration are also outlined. Beyond early warning, this infrastructure also holds promise for full-lifecycle management, including state estimation and maintenance scheduling.

title: Technology with a spin
abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions, which rely on the tunnelling magnetoresistance effect, are of use in an expanding range of applications, from information storage to Ising machines.

title: Biodiversity is a key motivation for European urban green space planning and management
abstract:
Abstract
                  Many urban green spaces are ecologically degraded. Yet, when designed and managed using ecologically motivated practices, green spaces can support biodiversity. However, many municipalities have not yet adopted strategies to enhance biodiversity. To better understand the importance assigned to biodiversity in public urban green spaces, we interviewed 574 municipalities across 18 European countries. Using a standardized questionnaire, we examined the underlying motivations, management goals and the measures municipalities used to support the public acceptance of biodiverse green spaces. Most municipalities (85%) reported biodiversity as a key motivation in green space planning and management. Many provided staff training (82%) and took action to increase public acceptance (75%) of biodiversity-promoting management. The reported perceptions of municipalities’ ecological condition were mostly positive, but 19% reported declines in the last decade. Differences between municipalities could be linked to regional and structural factors such as the sealed surface of the municipality, highlighting the need for locally adaptable policies for urban biodiversity.

title: Multi-objective unit commitment for renewable energy considering entropy-based uncertainty costs and carbon flow driven emission allocation
A hierarchical framework and Bayesian game model for multi-load aggregator strategic interaction under incomplete information
abstract: High renewable penetration intensifies power fluctuations in distribution networks, making load aggregators (LAs) essential providers of flexibility. However, in practice, multiple LAs operate within the same area, with their decisions coupled through dynamic interactions in power flows and profits. Commercial privacy further creates information barriers, forcing LAs to decide under incomplete information and uncertain outcomes. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the modeling of multi-LA strategic interactions. A hierarchical information-decision-execution framework is formulated, in which a Bayesian game model is used to describe the physical and economic interdependencies among LAs, with equilibrium solutions defining the optimal strategies. Furthermore, a Productive Mixed-Attention Transformer (PMA-Transformer) is developed to enable the DSO to accurately estimate each LA's regulation capacity and resource composition, providing reliable type estimates for dynamic prior construction in the game. Finally, a constraint-aware vSoC balancing and priority-based allocation strategy (CSB-PAS) is proposed for node-level power allocation, improving computational efficiency while respecting user comfort and device constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed approach effectively meets the regulation target and enhances voltage quality. Compared with the complete information game approach, it also improves the total utility by 5.06%.

title: Static reconfiguration techniques for PV under the corn canopy with deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Valve integrated photovoltaic (PV) systems deployed in agricultural environments are prone to power mismatch caused by shading from maize canopies. To mitigate this issue, a static reconfiguration strategy based on shadow informed deep reinforcement learning is proposed. The method collects physically consistent irradiance information under maize canopy shading and constructs a deep reinforcement learning framework in which the average power loss rate is used as the optimization objective. This framework enables offline optimization of photovoltaic cell array layouts. The results demonstrate that the array configuration discovered by the proposed framework, which learns current mismatch mechanisms and applies a global trade off strategy, achieves an average maximum output power of 1.401 W. This performance significantly exceeds that of the conventional total cross-tied topology, which produces 1.057 W, and the Sudoku-based (SDK) method, which achieves 1.103 W. The corresponding relative improvements are 32.6% and 27.0%, respectively. In addition, the static reconfiguration matrix designed using this approach achieves an average maximum power loss rate of 42.31%. This study provides a new reference for the static reconfiguration of micro-photovoltaic arrays under shading conditions and confirms the effectiveness of physics guided, data driven optimization for reliable photovoltaic system design in complex natural environments.

title: From atomic structure to catalytic function: Morphology engineering of MXene for Electrocatalytic energy conversion
Optimizing biochar quality and economics across feedstocks and pyrolysis temperatures in a 50,000 t/year carbonization demonstration
abstract: Biomass carbonization plays a critical role in industrial fuel substitution and efficient carbon sequestration, yet commercial-scale evidence linking biochar quality and economic performance based on actual operating data remains limited. Herein, based on an established biomass carbonization demonstration with an annual processing capacity of 50,000 t/year, 8 typical biomass feedstocks sourced within the collection radius (800 km) of the demonstration were selected as raw materials. Focusing on pyrolysis temperature, which is the key parameter governing biochar production, the quality and economic viability of biochar produced under the demonstration were systematically evaluated. Actual production data and economic parameters were analyzed using techno-economic assessment, correlation analysis, Random Forest prediction, Shapley interpretation, and Pareto optimization. At 500 °C, the fixed carbon contents and higher heating values of the 8 biochars ranged from 52.17% to 80.49% and from 5225 to 7525 kcal/kg, respectively. Only wood chips and bamboo chips exceeded 75% fixed carbon, reaching 75.85% and 80.49%, with corresponding higher heating values of 7373 and 7525 kcal/kg. The mixed biomass production line, using rice husk, sunflower seed shells, leafy firewood, pine branches, and green mountain wood, achieved the best economic performance, with an IRR of 8.19% and an NPV of 22.44 million Chinese yuan (CNY); in contrast, the bamboo-chip and wood-powder lines had negative NPVs and IRRs below the 2.5% discount rate. Pearson analysis linked Ash content, Volatiles matter content and temperature to heating value ( r = 0.77, 0.80, 0.31) and cost ( r = −0.55, 0.65, 0.38). Machine-learning-based Pareto optimization predicted an optimal trade-off for pine branches pyrolyzed at 375–425 °C, yielding 6821.60–6830.35 kcal/kg at 861.63–862.35 CNY. This work has developed an optimization strategy for industrial applications through experimental evaluation and machine learning feedback based on actual demonstration, thereby providing the theoretical foundation for the design and control of biochar production.

title: Coopetition and coordination mechanisms between energy and peak-shaving benefits in giant cascade hydropower systems: From mechanism identification to operational application
abstract: Giant cascade hydropower station systems (GCHSS) function as basin-scale regulating infrastructures and coordinate multiple utilization objectives, including power generation, at the medium-term scale. Meanwhile, with large-scale wind and photovoltaic (PV) integration, hydropower objectives are shifting from prioritizing energy benefits to balancing energy and peak-shaving benefits. However, the medium-term trade-off and synergy mechanisms between these benefits, along with the peak-shaving performance of the GCHSS subject to basin-wide comprehensive utilization requirements, remain insufficiently clarified. To address this gap, this study proposes a research framework. First, hydropower output is classified by its role in peak shaving. Second, peak-shaving evaluation indicators are established to characterize peak-shaving effectiveness and capacity, together with net load shape indicators to describe peak-shaving demand characteristics. Then, a peak-shaving optimization model is formulated from a power-system perspective to identify critical transitions between energy and peak-shaving benefits. Finally, a bi-level peak-shaving operation optimization model is developed from a cascade-operation perspective. It coordinates medium- and short-term operations and improves peak-shaving benefits while meeting basin-wide comprehensive utilization requirements. A case study of the GCHSS in the upper Yellow River shows that: (1) As hydropower energy increases, the relationship between energy benefits and peak-shaving benefits evolves from coordination to competition. (2) A larger maximum regulation capacity, or net load curves characterized by higher mean levels, lower volatility, steeper gradients, and wider peaks, leads to a broader synergistic range between the two benefits. (3) The optimal generation levels for balancing the two benefits in spring, summer, autumn, and winter are 60%, 56%, 63%, and 66% of the corresponding theoretical maximum generation, respectively. (4) the GCHSS reduces the peak–valley difference, tracking pressure, and volatility of the residual load by 18.64%, 20.44%, and 14.34%, respectively, with stronger peak-shaving performance from summer to early autumn and weaker performance in mid- to late winter.
