Synthesis of ammonia and its application in the sustainable steel process: A review
Quantifying the power system benefits of building upgrades for passive survivability in a changing climate
Mechanochemical crystallization of covalent organic frameworks: from the linkage up
abstract: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.

title: Using NMR to predict molecular reactivity
abstract: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.

title: Harnessing protein conformational dynamics for next-generation supramolecular materials
abstract: Protein conformational dynamics govern how proteins assemble across distinct pathways. This review unifies native crystallization, amyloid fibrillization, and reduction-induced phase transitions, revealing how dynamic assembly routes can be harnessed to design adaptive, hierarchical protein materials with programmable functions.

title: Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
Toward Robust InP Laser Lift-Off: Energy-Dependent Absorption Shift and Self-Absorption under Single-Pulse 1064 nm Irradiation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of InP on silicon is essential for the next generation of electronic systems by enabling high-performance photonics and radio frequency devices. Near-infrared Laser Lift-Off (LLO) is a promising route to enable the cost-effective transfer of InP-based device layers onto Si platforms. However, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To clarify these laser-material interactions, we investigate an InP/InGaAs heterostructure under single-pulse 1064 nm irradiation. Through microstructural characterization and coupled optical-thermal simulations, we reveal that the LLO process deviates fundamentally from the conventional sacrificial layer decomposition model. Instead, we identify an energy-dependent transition driven by highly localized transient melting and dynamic optical property changes. At moderate energies, rapid atomic intermixing and phosphorus depletion occur within a short-lived liquid phase, followed by epitaxial recrystallization that preserves macroscopic structural integrity. At higher energies, thermally induced bandgap shrinkage in the nominally transparent InP strongly enhances direct 1064 nm absorption. This initiates a positive feedback loop of thermal runaway, shifting the dominant energy absorption from the InGaAs sacrificial layer toward the InP layer and causing catastrophic ablation. These findings suggest that the onset of InP self-absorption imposes a critical high-energy constraint on the LLO process, rather than the sacrificial-layer decomposition threshold alone, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding and optimizing InP layer transfer.

title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
abstract: Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO2 separation.

title: Marine primary production enhances removal of hydrophobic organic contaminants from Eurasian Arctic shelf waters
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state‑of‑the‑art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate‑driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate‑induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

title: Global-scale variability of glacier velocity and mass loss across terminus environments
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang’e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

title: Tibetan Plateau uplift increased western North Pacific tropical cyclone frequency
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nearly one-third of global tropical cyclones (TCs) form over the western North Pacific (WNP), with severe hazards impacting Southeast and East Asia. TC genesis over the WNP underwent substantial shifts during the Cenozoic, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Tibetan Plateau uplift was crucial in shaping the present-day WNP TC genesis pattern. With the present-day land-sea configuration and sea surface temperature prescribed, Tibetan Plateau uplift from early Eocene to modern elevations accounts for nearly half of the simulated increase in TC frequency between the early Eocene and present day. Mechanistically, Tibetan Plateau uplift generates an eastward-propagating Rossby wave train, enhancing the WNP subtropical high and thereby intensifying the monsoon trough. The amplified moisture supply and reinforced upward motion within the monsoon trough collectively favor TC genesis and intensification. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of High Mountain Asia in the Cenozoic evolution of TC frequency over the WNP.

title: Climate-driven water stress in the United States is seasonal, regional, and shaped by adaptation
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: This study quantifies drivers of water use across the food-energy-water nexus and assesses how climate change, population growth, and adaptation may reshape future water scarcity in the United States. Using high frequency water withdrawal data from 2000–2020, we disentangle the effects of climate, hydrology, and socioeconomic factors on public water use, crop irrigation, and cooling for thermoelectric power generation. Future water demands (2040–2070) are estimated using recent climate and socioeconomic projections, representing 1.0 ∘C to 2.9 ∘C warming and population growth ranging from 1% to 44%. Across 28 scenarios, we estimate annual water use changes ranging from -10.7% to +28.9% for public use, +32.1% to +43.6% for crop irrigation, and -27.9% to -19.9% for thermoelectric power cooling, contingent on continued adaptive efforts. Results reveal strong sectoral variation in climate sensitivity, seasonal mismatches between water supply and demand, and shifts in regional water stress under future warming.

title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
abstract: Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance.

title: Climate warming boosts frequency and intensity of southern Africa’s rainfall extremes
abstract: Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone (a major source of rainfall across southern Africa) can trigger devastating floods. Climate-model projections indicate that these swings might occur twice as often in the twenty-first century as in the previous century and produce more intense rainfall, owing to an increased land–sea temperature contrast and poleward intensification of atmospheric circulation.

title: Giant orbital Zeeman effects in a magnetic topological van der Waals interphase
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic ‘interphases’ may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g-factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2. They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe3GeTe2, producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

title: Isolation of uranocenium, the bis-[8]annulene uranium cation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Uranocene, [UIV(η8-C8H8)2], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [UV(η8-C8H8)2]+, and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron–electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U–C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

title: Force-driven single-molecule transformations through tip-mediated stabilization of transition states
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

title: Singularity-free supertwisted atomic layers with giant circular dichroisms
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Supertwisted van der Waals (vdW) multilayers—in which layers are stacked with identical interlayer twist angles—enable strong and programmable chiral light–matter interactions. However, directly synthesizing these multilayers remains challenging, as the conventional growth process typically produces supertwisted spirals containing an inevitable central singularity and substantial in-plane strain. Here, we demonstrate the growth of singularity-free supertwisted WS2 multilayers by employing a dome-shaped WS2 monolayer as a pre-deposited template. The crack line that forms on the dome acts as a dislocation line, with its two termini serving as a conjugate pair of opposite-handed screw dislocations. This configuration enables a dislocation-guided, layer-by-layer growth process that is free of topological singularities and characterized by low residual strain. The multilayers exhibit giant chiroptical responses, including a linear-optical circular dichroism (CD) of up to 10 mdeg and a second-harmonic CD of 0.81 within an ultrathin thickness of ~ 6 nm. Our work provides an effective route for growth of supertwisted multilayers and presents a programmable platform for chiral photonics.

title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet flat optics are constrained by undersampling of steep edge phase gradients, which reduces phase fidelity and high-angle diffraction efficiency. Here, we introduce a momentum-relay architecture that partitions large wavevector deflections across two cascaded elements. A 4:1 demagnification platform operating at 532 nm synthesizes an effective numerical aperture of 0.80, producing a measured first-dark-ring radius of 413.2 nm and resolving ~555 nm image-plane features across a 100 μm-diameter field of view. We further translate the concept to 13.24 nm using a compact xenon laser-produced-plasma source. Two Fresnel zone plates, each with a numerical aperture of approximately 0.33, cooperatively synthesize an effective numerical aperture of approximately 0.53. Here, we show that cascaded momentum relay provides a compact route to high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet projection while relaxing the feature-size and spatial-sampling requirements imposed on each element.

title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10−5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X/2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10−6. We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

title: Interfacial Hydrogen Spillover in Partially Alloyed PdNi Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen spillover can decouple elementary steps in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet conventional bimetallic catalysts often suffer from discontinuous interfaces that block spillover pathways. Herein, an interfacial hydrogen spillover mechanism is engineered in a Pd–PdNi–Ni catalyst via a partial interface alloying strategy for pH‐universal hydrogen evolution. The graded PdNi interface serves as a recombination sink integrating two synergistic pathways: primary spillover, in which strongly adsorbed H* generated on Ni spontaneously migrates across the interface, and secondary spillover, in which H* produced on Pd also diffuses to the same interfacial sites. The dual spillover is driven by a favorable hydrogen intermediate gradient resulting from Ni‐to‐Pd electron transfer and an optimized d‐band center. The optimal catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 60 mV (alkaline) and 37 mV (acidic) at 10 mA cm −2 , with robust durability, and the corresponding anion exchange membrane electrolyzer exhibits 1.73 V at 0.5 A cm −2 and 452 h stability in simulated seawater. Operando Raman spectroscopy detects Pd–H and Ni–H vibrations, providing direct evidence for hydrogen migration from both domains to the interface, and theoretical calculations confirm the electronic origin and spillover pathways. This work demonstrates a rational design for high‐performance HER catalysts by harnessing dual hydrogen spillover.

title: Recyclable flow battery chemistry
abstract: Turning water-based flow batteries into a truly sustainable technology hinges on recycling the organic molecules inside the battery. A redox-active organic molecule has now been developed that not only outperforms the industry-standard vanadium benchmark but also offers exceptional reusability.

title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

title: Illusory disagreement over socialism and capitalism in the United States and Brazil
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Capitalism and socialism offer starkly contrasting visions of how wealth and power should be acquired within society. For Americans today, this appears to be a fundamental ideological conflict, as most self-identified Democrats report positive views of socialism, while most self-identified Republicans report negative views. Across five studies (N = 1753), including four pre-registered experiments (N = 1640), we provide evidence that this divide is overestimated. In Studies 1-4, we find that Americans broadly support a hybrid economic system that combines elements of capitalism and socialism, but they apply different labels—either “capitalist” or “socialist”—depending on their political ideologies. We show that highlighting these shared values reduces perceptions of intergroup differences and enhances receptiveness to outparty policies. Highlighting these shared values also increases support for outparty candidates who support (1) a social safety net that provides everyone food, clean water, basic healthcare, and shelter, (2) investments in public education and programs that develop skills, (3) a progressive tax system, and (4) regulations to ensure that free markets protect consumers and the environment. These effects were significant for both Republicans and Democrats and persisted for at least one month. In Study (5), we replicate this pattern in Brazil, as Brazilians also largely agree on a shared economic system but apply different labels depending on their political ideologies. These findings demonstrate the potential to reduce partisan divides by revealing hidden agreement concerning the fundamental economic structure of society.

title: High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

title: Quantifying Sodium Metal SEI Dissolution and Relation to Corrosion Using Quartz Crystal Microbalance
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.

title: Weak-Solvating Carboxylate Ester Electrolyte Enables Hybrid Interphase via Cooperative Additives toward Wide-Temperature Sodium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.

title: A thin carbon membrane to capture carbon
abstract: Anthropogenic emissions are rapidly increasing atmospheric CO2 levels, with severe consequences for the global climate. Researchers have developed a carbon membrane as thin as only two molecular layers that sieves and captures CO2 with very high flux and selectivity, holding promise for climate change mitigation technologies.

title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, affects an estimated 10.5 million people worldwide and remains a leading cause of infectious cardiomyopathy in Latin America. Although infection is lifelong without treatment, only 20–30% of chronically infected individuals progress from an asymptomatic stage to clinically significant cardiac disease, and current antiparasitic therapies are limited by toxicity and variable efficacy. Reliable biomarkers capable of predicting disease progression would improve clinical risk stratification and support therapeutic development. Here, we performed a metabolomics study to identify serum biomarkers predictive of progression from asymptomatic infection to cardiac CD. Untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry profiling using complementary chromatographic platforms and univariate statistics, machine learning feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to identify candidate biomarkers. These biomarkers were validated by targeted analysis. We identified eight individual metabolite biomarkers and 45 combinatorial panels predictive of progression status, including 10 panels that met sensitivity and specificity criteria defined in the target product profile for CD treatment-response biomarkers. These findings demonstrate that circulating metabolites measured at baseline can predict future cardiac disease progression and provide a foundation for clinically deployable prognostic tools in chronic Chagas disease.

title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: OSTα/β is the essential basolateral transporter responsible for returning reabsorbed bile acids to the portal circulation, yet its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human OSTα/β at 2.7 Å resolution, revealing a 7-TM architecture distinct from all established SLC transporter folds. We further determined the taurocholate (TC)-bound structure at 3.2 Å, showing that the substrate laterally binds to a surface groove on OSTα, but not in the central cavity. The TC molecule is captured by a line of conserved polar residues along the groove, which were further proved by structure-guided mutagenesis combined with transport assays. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that it is energetically favored for TC moving along the surface groove. Together, structural analysis, functional assays, and simulations demonstrate that OSTα/β mediates bile acid transmembrane translocation via a facilitated lateral diffusion mechanism with subtle conformational change, which is distinct from known SLCs. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for OSTα/β function in enterohepatic bile acid circulation and provide a foundation for therapeutic modulation of bile acid homeostasis.

title: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) drive cancer initiation and progression but remain “undruggable” due to formidable challenges in rescuing the functional impairment of heterogeneous truncated proteins with a single agent. Here we observe that suppressor transfer RNAs (sup-tRNAs) can overcome diverse nonsense mutations in TP53, restoring full-length p53 expression and function. Sup-tRNAs enable high-fidelity incorporation of optimal amino acids and can further enhance the transcriptional activity of p53 to suppress tumour cell proliferation. Moreover, we employ a computational model to guide sup-tRNA design by in silico saturation mutagenesis for targeted readthrough of different nonsense-mutant TSGs. Remarkably, sup-tRNAs produced p53 variants with enhanced activity relative to restored wild-type p53, reducing cancer cell colony area by up to 82%. In two xenograft models harbouring nonsense mutant TP53, we observed up to a 74% reduction in tumour volume after lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based sup-tRNA treatment, attributed to robust recovery of p53 expression and function. Critically, sup-tRNA monotherapy surpassed nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy in efficacy, and their combination induced near-complete tumour regression (a maximum of 93% reduction in tumour volume) without detectable toxicity in multiple mouse tumour models. Our findings highlight the potential of tRNA-based therapy to provide a promising strategy for rescuing nonsense-mutant TP53.

title: Unveiling the functional specialisation of human white matter circuits with naturalistic stimuli
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

title: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS.

title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Orthobunyaviruses, an important group of arboviruses with broad vector and host ranges, pose a persistent global public health threat, yet their cellular entry and cross-species transmission remain poorly understood. Ebinur Lake virus (EBIV), a recently identified orthobunyavirus detected in multiple countries and hosts, demonstrates potential zoonotic and spillover relevance. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify discoidin domain receptor 2 (DDR2) as an entry receptor for EBIV. Knockout and ectopic expression confirm that DDR2 promotes EBIV infectivity by facilitating viral binding and internalization. The discoidin (DS) domain of DDR2 directly interacts with EBIV particles at the Gc stalk region. A soluble DS decoy or anti-DDR2 DS antibody potently inhibits EBIV infection in cell lines and primary neural cells. The DS decoy or Ddr2 knockout protects mice from lethal EBIV challenge, significantly reducing viral loads. DDR2 homologs from diverse mammals and birds bind EBIV Gc and support infection, underscoring a broad host range. Notably, we demonstrate a receptor switch among phylogenetically related orthobunyaviruses: human-infecting Germiston virus (GERV) also utilizes DDR2, while Bozo virus (BOZOV) employs DDR1. These findings establish discoidin domain receptors as functional entry receptors for orthobunyaviruses, revealing a mechanism for broad host tropism and providing insights for antiviral strategies.

title: Tom70–mediated mitochondria–nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD–CD27–CD11c+CD21– B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation. Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.

title: LUBAC PUB domain interactions restrict Met1-linked ubiquitination to prevent murine embryonic lethality and immune pathology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Met1-linked ubiquitin assembled by LUBAC coordinates immune receptor signalling and inflammation. The PUB domain of the LUBAC subunit HOIP interacts with PUB-interacting motif-containing proteins, including the deubiquitinases OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Yet, how these interactions regulate LUBAC remains unclear. Here, we investigate the consequences of ablating PUB-interacting motif interactions by generating mice carrying an N101D mutation in the HOIP PUB domain. The N101D mutation causes embryonic lethality at mid-gestation driven partly by TNF receptor 1 but not solely by the loss of interaction with OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Mutation of the HOIP PUB domain causes Met1-linked autoubiquitination without inhibiting LUBAC activity, leading to superfluous Met1-linked ubiquitination of TNF receptor complex components after TNF, resulting in impaired gene activation and increased cell death. In adult mice, the N101D mutation causes cytokine storm, immune dysregulation, and weight loss. We report the HOIP PUB domain as a critical protein-interaction interface regulating LUBAC function in receptor signalling and immune homoeostasis.

title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

title: Magnetic Resonance Reveals Radical Stability in Native Biofilms and Its Role in Bacterial Resistance
abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial cells embedded in biofilms exhibit enhanced antimicrobial resistance compared with planktonic cells, contributing to persistent infections and failure of conventional antibiotic treatments. This resistance is influenced by the extracellular matrix (ECM), a heterogeneous network of polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids surrounding embedded cells. However, how the ECM regulates the accessibility of redox‐active small molecules remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), solid‐state NMR (ssNMR), and dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) ssNMR to determine how native Pseudomonas fluorescens Pf0‐1 colony biofilms differentially reduce nitroxide radicals across morphologies. EPR reveals that radical reduction depends on biofilm morphology, hydration, and ECM composition. Wild‐type biofilms exhibit slower nitroxide reduction than planktonic cells, while isolated ECM and dehydrated biofilms show negligible reduction, highlighting the importance of cellular accessibility. ssNMR identifies preferential spatial proximity of nitroxides to ECM polysaccharides and lipids, while DNP ssNMR reveals increasing polysaccharide content across biofilm morphologies that correlates with slower reduction kinetics. These findings support a model of protection in which the ECM provides the barrier to nitroxide access, and cellular reduction is the final step. Our integrated magnetic resonance approach provides molecular insight into how biofilm composition and structure determine the fate of therapeutically relevant redox‐active small molecules.

title: Fluxional Monomers Remodel Crystallinity at Low Loadings in Diketopyrrolopyrrole Co‐Thienothiophene Conjugated Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conjugated polymers (CPs) are a class of semiconducting materials in which electrical conductivity and mechanical extensibility can coincide. Despite advances in synthesis and processing, these key properties are typically negatively correlated and derive from the semicrystalline microstructure of the polymer film. Here, we introduce a new strategy to improve the microstructure and mechanical properties of CPs through the introduction of bullvalene‐based fluxional comonomers, in which bonds rearrange constantly at ambient temperatures. By comparing bullvalene‐containing poly(diketopyrrolopyrrole‐thienothiophene) (p(DPP‐TT)) with static controls, we show that fluxional backbones resist thermal annealing induced crystallization, creating smaller crystallites even at low comonomer loadings (5 mol%). While comonomers produce minimal mechanical differences in low‐molecular weight CPs, when the network is reinforced through crosslinking, bullvalene strongly enhances stretchability, yielding a crack onset strain more than twice that of the controls. Additional experiments indicate that crosslinking enables the network to realign micro crystallites under stress to delay crack onset, but only when large crystallites are absent, as in fluxional CPs. Despite the incorporation of non‐conjugated comonomers, electrical mobility remains similar to controls at all levels of strain. This work demonstrates that fluxional components can outperform static analogues as structural modifiers in diketopyrrolopyrrole co‐thienothiophene CPs, leading to significant macroscopic effects.

title: Surfactant‐Mediated “ Oil‐in‐Water ” Electrolyte Design via Sonochemical Assembly: Low‐Dielectric Interfacial Regulation for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐metal batteries are plagued by severe performance degradation originating from the Zn anode's instability. Although electrolyte engineering has been widely established as a primary strategy to address this challenge, the utility of numerous promising species is intrinsically limited by their poor aqueous solubility. Herein, a surfactant‐mediated “ oil‐in‐water ” (denoted as SMOW) electrolyte design is proposed to unlock the potential of hydrophobic species. A long‐term stable micellar electrolyte is developed via sonochemically engineered self‐assembly, in which hydrophobic species are encapsulated within the surfactant micelles. Driven by interfacial electrostatic repulsion, these micelles release the hydrophobic species on the zinc anode surface. The enriched interfacial layer acts as an effective low‐dielectric shield, intrinsically accelerating Zn 2+ desolvation while physically isolating the Zn anode from reactive water molecules. Owing to the synergistic effect between the hydrophobic species and the surfactant, highly compact and dendrite‐free Zn deposition with suppressed parasitic side reactions is realized, enabling an ultralong cycling lifespan of over 3900 h for the Zn anode at 10 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the assembled Zn||I 2 full cells deliver cycling for over 10000 cycles at 5 A g −1 with negligible capacity fading. This work provides a universal paradigm to break through the design constraints of aqueous electrolytes.

title: Cross-Dimensional Percolation and Metastructure-Assisted Highly Efficient Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Increasing electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues make shielding materials urgent in need. However, designing a thin/lightweight material with high shielding effectiveness (SE over 100 dB) by facile and scalable technologies with high production accuracy is still challenging. Herein, excellent shielding composite films are successfully prepared through sequential scalable positive pressure filtration, accurate inkjet printing, and facile transferring. From mass ratio optimization of 1D silver nanowires to 2D MXene, a skeleton with maximum inner free space and fast electron and phonon transport channels through cross-dimensional percolation is produced for internal multiple reflection absorption. To further increase EMI SE, graphene-based mesh metamaterials are theoretically calculated and accurately printed with controlled conductivity for impedance matching as the top layer. Facile inkjet printing succeeds in balancing print accuracy and conductivity control by advanced ink formulation. Finally, under multiple attenuation mechanisms verified through complex permittivity analysis in both frequency domain and real space (conductive loss, dipole polarization, and various interfacial polarizations), EMI SE of 102.31 dB in X-band is achieved. Integrating different attenuation technologies in a single material system of multidimensions inspires further designing shielding materials with increasingly strict requirements like multiband compatibility with special frequency enhancement.

title: Hansen Solubility-Guided Design Optimization of Biopolymer–Drug Compatibility for Photodynamically Antimicrobial Biomaterials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Designing polymeric nanocarriers for hydrophobic therapeutics requires an understanding of polymer–drug interactions and their dependence on polymer molecular weight. Herein, poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) oligomers (αPBS) with tunable molecular weights were prepared via controlled microwave-assisted alcoholysis to investigate the relationships among molecular weight, solubility behavior, and curcumin encapsulation. Experimental solubility mapping revealed substantial deviations between experimentally determined and conventionally predicted Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) in the oligomeric regime, highlighting the limitations of group-contribution methods for low-molecular-weight polyesters. The PBS oligomer with a M̅n of approximately 2,000 g/mol (αPBS6) exhibited experimental HSP values of δD = 17.0, δP = 7.3, and δH = 7.1 MPa½. Despite borderline-to-unfavorable HSP-derived compatibility with curcumin (RED ≈ 1.04 and χ ≈ 1.21), αPBS6 exhibited high curcumin encapsulation, demonstrating that HSP-derived parameters alone do not directly predict encapsulation efficiency. Curcumin-loaded αPBS nanoparticles (Cur@PBS6) had an average diameter of 232 ± 1.5 nm, a high loading capacity (8.54–9.10%), and good colloidal stability. Their loading capacity exceeded those of commercial PBS (6.36%), PBSA (6.64%), and PLA (2.75%) systems, indicating that molecular-weight modification and nanoparticle formation conditions contribute to curcumin incorporation. Spectroscopic analyses suggested reduced curcumin aggregation following encapsulation, which preserved its photoactivity and promoted reactive oxygen species generation under blue-light irradiation. Moreover, Cur@PBS6-incorporated electrospun poly(lactic acid) fibers exhibited photodynamic antibacterial activity under blue-light irradiation (450 nm, 0.3 W/cm2, 60 min), achieving bacterial killing efficiencies of 94.2% against Escherichia coli and 98.1% against Staphylococcus aureus. These findings demonstrate that experimentally determined HSPs provide a complementary framework for evaluating molecular-weight-dependent polymer–drug interactions, while nanocarrier performance is collectively governed by molecular weight, crystallinity, formulation condition, and other physicochemical factors.

title: Manganese-Coordinated Rhein Hydrogel as a Vaccine Adjuvant for Synergistically Enhanced Humoral and Cellular Immunity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Manganese ions (Mn2+), which act as agonists of the cGAS-STING pathway, hold considerable promise as vaccine adjuvants. However, free Mn2+ is rapidly cleared after injection, making it difficult to sustain local immune stimulation. In this study, we exploited the coordination between Mn2+ and rhein, a naturally occurring anthraquinone small molecule, to construct a novel injectable Rhe@Mn hydrogel through one-step self-assembly. Within the hydrogel, densely packed supramolecular nanofibers intertwine to form a three-dimensional network, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the uniform distribution of Mn along the nanofibers. Rheological testing showed that the Rhe@Mn hydrogel had favorable viscoelasticity and structural stability. In vitro studies, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel retained the STING-agonist activity of Mn2+ and effectively promoted antigen uptake by DCs and their maturation. In vivo, the hydrogel formed an antigen depot at the injection site, enabling sustained antigen release for up to 10 days. It also efficiently recruited immune cells, including DCs and macrophages, thereby establishing a local immune microenvironment enriched in antigen-presenting cells. After a single immunization, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel vaccine increased the abundance of germinal-center B (GC B) cells in lymph nodes by approximately 3.7-fold, significantly enhanced antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses, and established durable immune memory. This study provides a facile, functionally integrated platform for adjuvant-antigen co-delivery in subunit vaccines.

title: Slide-Ring Hydrogel Networks Cross-Linked by Movable Cucurbit[8]uril/Macromer Host-Guest Complexes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract For traditional covalently cross-linked hydrogels, achieving both stiffness and toughness is generally difficult, owing to the fixed cross-linking points and the lack of dynamic response. Introducing movable cross-linking points into the network has proven to be an effective strategy to overcome this limitation. However, most existing approaches rely on pseudopolyrotaxane architectures based on cyclodextrin (CD) and polyethylene glycol (PEG), which require complicated synthesis. In this study, slide-ring hydrogels were conveniently synthesized via free radical polymerization of acrylamide (AM) and acrylic acid (AA) monomers, employing a supramolecular complex of azobenzene guest-modified telechelic macromers (Acr-Azo-PEG20K-Azo-Acr) and cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) as movable cross-linkers. Benefiting from the introduction of dynamic host–guest cross-linking, these hydrogels possess movable cross-linking points that can effectively dissipate energy and distribute stress during deformation, thereby significantly enhancing the mechanical properties through the pulley effect. By tuning the cross-linker content, solid content, and monomer structure, the material properties could be precisely optimized. Furthermore, posttreatment with ferric citrate (FeCA) allowed the introduction of Fe3+ dynamic coordination cross-linking into the acrylic-based slide-ring hydrogels, achieving a simultaneous 3-fold increase in tensile strength and an approximately 4-fold increase in toughness while maintaining high ductility and excellent fatigue resistance. The use of macromer/CB[8] complexes as movable cross-linkers offers a new strategy for high-performance hydrogels and lays a solid foundation for their future applications.

title: Nanostructure-Enabled Apparent Slip through Dynamic Hydration Reorganization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dynamic transport across solid–liquid nanointerfaces is commonly interpreted through equilibrium wettability, although increasing evidence suggests that interfacial hydration rather than contact angle governs nanoscale liquid motion. However, how hydration reorganizes under ionic and hydrodynamic perturbations at strongly hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that dendritic silica nanostructures create a hydration-rich interphase whose dynamic mechanical state can be programmed by electrolyte concentration, flow, and biomolecular adsorption. Contact-angle measurements, density functional theory calculations, and overtone-resolved quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring reveal that intermediate ionic strengths maximize near-surface acoustic loading without a proportional increase in dissipation, while increasing flow induces a flow-dependent enhancement in model-derived apparent mobility. The response is strongest at higher overtones and persists after bovine serum albumin adsorption, demonstrating that the adaptive hydration state survives the formation of a complex protein–water interphase. Rather than reflecting the classical hydrophobic slip, the observations identify a dynamically reconfigurable hydration layer that decouples equilibrium wettability from interfacial mechanics. These findings establish hydration-layer reconfigurability as a general mechanism governing liquid mobility at hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces and provide a design framework for nanofluidic transport, antifouling materials, separation membranes, and interfacial biosensing technologies.

title: Integrated Droplet Microfluidic Platform for Single-Spheroid Photothermal Nanotherapy and Morphology-Driven Response Prediction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a promising cancer treatment modality, but its evaluation remains limited by the lack of physiologically relevant and quantitatively controlled in vitro platforms. Here, we present a droplet-based microfluidic platform that enables single-spheroid formation, programmable nanoparticle delivery, and in situ laser irradiation with real-time thermal monitoring. The platform enables temperature multiplexing within a single experiment, allowing construction of single-spheroid dose–response relationships and the definition of a temperature-based inhibitory metric (IT50). This provides a direct and physically meaningful quantification of photothermal efficacy. In parallel, a label-free, spheroid morphology-based machine learning approach predicts treatment response across cell types, nanoparticle incubation conditions, and therapeutic regimes while preserving intrinsic single-spheroid variability. Despite a limited dataset size and biological heterogeneity, the system achieves robust and reproducible predictive performance. Overall, this work establishes a scalable and versatile microfluidic framework for quantitative photothermal nanotherapy screening, integrating controlled thermal dosing, 3D tumor models, and morphological data-driven analysis within a single-spheroid platform.

title: Amino-Terminated Ti3C2T x MXene Prepared via Ammonia Treatment Boosts Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Defect-mediated non-radiative recombination and progressive material degradation impose fundamental limits on the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational durability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, we synthesized amino-terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene (denoted as A-MXene) nanosheets through LiF/HCl etching and subsequent ammonia post-treatment and incorporated them into PSCs. Characterization results reveal that ammonia treatment modifies the surface/interlayer chemistry of Ti3C2Tx and introduces amino-related nitrogen species, accompanied by increased interlayer spacing, reduced lateral flake dimensions, and enhanced dispersibility. In PSCs, A-MXene regulates both Pb- and I-related chemical environments, improves perovskite crystallization, suppresses non-radiative recombination, and promotes interfacial hole extraction. Consequently, the A-MXene-modified device delivers a PCE of 23.49%. Moreover, the encapsulated device retains 94.9% of its initial PCE after 720 h of uninterrupted 1-sun illumination at 85 °C in a N2 atmosphere. These findings establish ammonia-treated MXene as a versatile additive capable of concurrently governing defect chemistry and charge transport, thereby enabling high-efficiency, stable PSCs.

title: Microstructured Ionic Polymer-Based Multifunctional Iontronic Skin for Pressure Sensing, Object Recognition, and Underwater Environmental Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Skin-like iontronic sensors capable of multifunctional sensing and reliable operation hold strong potential for next-generation wearable electronics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and multifunctionality within a single platform remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a multifunctional iontronic skin based on a microstructured ionic polymer (MSiP) composed of PVDF and [EMIM]+[BF4]– ion pairs. The MSiP is fabricated through mask-less photolithography to create highly ordered micropillar arrays with a diameter of 30 μm, a height of 5 μm, and an interspacing of 20 μm. The iontronic skin is constructed by sandwiching the MSiP layer between flexible PDMS/PEDOT:PSS electrodes, where pressure-induced migration of highly mobile [BF4]– ions, as revealed by molecular dynamics simulations, facilitates electrical double-layer formation at the MSiP/electrode interface, resulting in enhanced capacitive response. Moreover, finite-element simulations reveal that the microstructured architecture effectively concentrates local stress, increases the effective contact area, and amplifies structural deformation during compression, thereby accounting for the exceptional pressure sensitivity of the MSiP sensor. As a result, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh pressure sensitivity of 833 kPa–1, a highly linear response (R2 = 0.98), and excellent durability over 20,000 loading–unloading cycles. Its remarkable sensitivity enables the detection of pressures as low as 3 Pa. Furthermore, integration with a robotic arm enables the development of a tactile robotic interface platform capable of real-time object grasping, lifting, and releasing in response to tactile forces applied to the sensor surface. The sensor can also be attached to the human body to monitor physiological signals and various body movements. Beyond tactile sensing, when combined with machine learning, the sensor can accurately distinguish objects ranging from soft cloth to rigid steel bottles, achieving a high classification accuracy of 95–97%. The iontronic sensor also demonstrates underwater sensing, including monitoring of depth (0–35 cm), temperature (20–80 °C), and salinity (0–8 ppt). This work presents a versatile iontronic platform that enables high-performance multifunctional sensing for wearable electronics, intelligent robotics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater environmental monitoring.

title: Enhanced Performance of Protonic Ceramic Electrolysis Cells via Transient Sinterlayer Engineering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Protonic ceramic electrolysis cells (PCECs) are a promising technology for efficient hydrogen production at intermediate temperatures (500–600 °C), but their commercialization is hindered by fabrication challenges. In particular, the high-temperature sintering required to densify barium cerate–zirconate electrolytes promotes barium volatilization, leading to phase decomposition and degraded performance. Here, we introduce a transient sinterlayer processing strategy in which a thin (∼1 μm) surface coating is applied atop the electrolyte before sintering. During high-temperature processing, the sinterlayer suppresses electrolyte decomposition, promotes densification and grain growth, and is ultimately incorporated into the perovskite lattice, yielding a chemically uniform perovskite electrolyte. Three sinterlayer compositions (CeO2, La2O3, and La2Ce2O7) were evaluated for BaCe0.7Zr0.1Y0.1Yb0.1O3–δ electrolytes. La2O3 provided the greatest benefit by enhancing grain growth, preserving dopant distributions, and substantially improving stability upon exposure to boiling water, although degradation under CO2-containing conditions at 550 °C remained evident. Integrated into complete electrolysis cells, La2O3 sinterlayers increased current density by 67.2% at 1.3 V and 600 °C while improving Faradaic efficiency from 78.8 to 85.0% relative to a bare cell. These results establish transient sinterlayers as an effective fabrication strategy for high-performance PCECs.

title: Prepressed Liquid Metal Fabric with Strain-Insensitive Conductance for Wearable Bioelectronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of flexible conductors with high electrical conductivity, flexibility, and electromechanical stability is important for reliable signal transmission in wearable electronics. Here, we report a patternable liquid metal (LM) fabric with strain-insensitive performance, fabricated using a highly elastic knitted fabric (KF) as the substrate and a gallium-based liquid metal as the conductive coating. A patterned poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) intermediate layer was introduced to enhance the interfacial adhesion and facilitate the selective deposition of LM on the textile substrate. In addition, pre‑oxidation of the LM followed by a prepressing treatment further promotes the permeation of liquid metal into the knitted fabric, thereby improving the stability of electrical conductivity. Benefiting from the pore structure of the fabric and the strong interfacial combination of liquid metal and PEDOT:PSS, this composite fabric achieves a strain capacity of 200% with low resistance variations, and the resistance change rates are 18.6% for longitudinal stretching, 20.4% for 45° diagonal stretching, and 24.8% for transverse stretching. When stretched by 100% along three distinct directions (transverse, longitudinal, and 45°), the resistance change rate remains below 5% in all cases, demonstrating excellent multidirectional strain-insensitive conductivity. Moreover, after 1000 cyclic stretching cycles under a 30% strain, the resistance fluctuation still stays within 3%. The resulting fabric exhibited excellent conductivity stability when applied to conductors, Joule heating, electrocardiogram (ECG), and near field communication (NFC), demonstrating its potential for next‑generation wearable electronics.

title: Energy policy and energy poverty under geopolitical fragmentation: Evidence on structural constraints
Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

Architecting Co-continuous PVDF Composites via Multi-material 3D Parallel Printing for Enhanced Piezoelectricity and Wearable Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites have attracted considerable attention for self-powered sensing; however, achieving efficient electromechanical response while maintaining structural integrity under repeated deformation remains challenging. Herein, a structure-driven multi-material 3D parallel printing strategy is developed to construct polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based piezoelectric composites with a co-continuous dual-phase architecture. In this design, ionic liquid (IL)-modified PVDF serves as the piezoelectric phase, where the IL promotes β-phase formation and dipole orientation, while carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-reinforced PVDF provides a conductive phase for electrical signal collection. Unlike conventional stacked configurations, the parallel-printed architecture enables continuous integration of the piezoelectric and conductive phases, providing intimate interfacial contact and a mechanically interconnected structure. The resulting structural continuity facilitates stress transfer during mechanical deformation and contributes to a stable electromechanical response. Kelvin probe force microscopy measurements further reveal an interfacial potential difference of 85.6 mV, indicating distinct interfacial electrical characteristics between the two phases. The optimized sensor delivers an output voltage of 0.55 V at 5 N, a sensitivity of 439.77 mV/N in the low-force regime, and a response time of 28 ms, together with excellent mechanical stability. Finite element analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced piezoelectric response is closely associated with the continuous deformation and effective stress transfer enabled by the parallel architecture. The sensor further exhibits reliable performance in human-motion monitoring and human–machine interaction. This work establishes multi-material 3D parallel printing as a structure-engineering approach for integrating piezoelectric and conductive phases and provides a versatile route toward high-performance flexible piezoelectric sensing devices.

title: A High-Brightness, Low-Energy-Spread Au Needle Point Electron Source Nanocold-Cathode Adapted to Low-Power Photoelectric Coexcitation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract To address the requirements of vacuum electronic and optoelectronic device applications for next-generation low-power-consumption, high-brightness, low-energy-spread, and tunable electron sources, the pursuit of high-efficiency metal nanocold-cathodes with plasmon-enhanced properties in specific waveband emerges as one of potent solutions. In this study, by screening and comparing the cathode materials and structures, we propose a high-brightness, low-energy-spread Au needle nanocold-cathode point electron source adapted to low-intensity photoelectric coexcitation. The experimental results demonstrate sensitivity to excitation light and outstanding electron emission performance of this point electron source: under the coexcitation of an electrostatic field below ∼1.25 V μm–1 and a supercontinuum-spectrum laser with average intensity of ∼24 W cm–2, the source achieved an emission current of 130 nA, improving by one order of magnitude when compared to the field emission current (∼13 nA) under pure electrostatic field excitation. As the laser excitation intensity increased, its effective work function decreased from 5.1 to 2.7 eV, resulting in a significant reduction of the excitation threshold for electron emission. Benefiting from the plasmon-enhanced light-harvesting effect, the cathode exhibits high sensitivity and selectivity to the wavelength and polarization of the incident light. In the 532–675 nm plasmon resonance band, the emission current exceeds 225 nA at an average excitation intensity of only 7.05 W cm–2, ∼17 times the pure electrostatic field emission current. Meanwhile, the plasmon relaxation preferentially populates high-energy electrons and suppresses the energy spread broadening induced by the space charge effect, thereby achieving a high reduced brightness of 6.89 × 109 A m–2 sr–1 V–1 and a low-energy spread of approximately 0.5 eV. This low-power photoelectric coexcitation scheme greatly relaxes the requirements on the excitation source, providing a route for the miniaturization and integration of vacuum optoelectronic point electron sources.

title: Growth Kinetics of Gallium Selenide on Graphene: Bridging Atomistic and Mesoscale Processes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving uniform, wafer-scale thin layers and heterostructures remains a major challenge in the synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors, which requires precise control of growth parameters and atomic-level insight into surface interactions. We combine density functional theory (DFT) and kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations to investigate the early stages of 2D gallium selenide (GaSe) growth on graphene and determine how GaSe domain morphology, growth rate, and nucleation density depend on the atomic fluxes and substrate temperature. The presence of Ga on the substrate is key to promoting GaSe nucleation, while a sufficiently high Se flux is required to enable 2D GaSe growth and suppress accumulation of Ga clusters. The DFT-informed KMC simulations also reveal a trade-off between the growth rate and morphology, showing that increasing the flux of Ga relative to Se promotes faster growth of GaSe and increases the surface roughness. In contrast, high substrate temperatures promote edge healing and favor the formation of compact triangular domains. These results identify a narrow window of experimental conditions for 2D GaSe growth on graphene.

title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

title: Disorder Beats Order: Carbon Microstructure Steers Radical Versus Cationic Pathways in Kolbe Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon electrodes are ubiquitous in organic electrochemistry, yet the structural origin of their selectivity in radical‐mediated reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that carbon microstructure is a primary determinant of product selectivity in Kolbe electrolysis, a prototypical electrochemical C─C coupling reaction central to fuel, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical production. We investigated eight carbon electrodes in two complementary libraries: five commercial carbons spanning diverse macroarchitectures, and carbon nanofibers with controlled graphitization. Both reveal a consistent structure–selectivity trend for various carboxylic acids and a mixed‐acid feed. Counterintuitively, the most disordered electrodes, despite the highest charge‐transfer resistance, give about an order of magnitude more Kolbe dimer than highly graphitized ones, which give little or none. Disordered, sp 3 ‐rich surfaces bearing oxygen functionalities strongly favor both Kolbe coupling (alkane) and Hofer–Moest products (alcohol/aldehyde), whereas graphitized, sp 2 ‐rich surfaces favor further oxidation to carbocations, yielding mainly alkenes and esters. Density functional theory calculations suggest that oxygen‐functionalized sites bind the alkyl radical about three times more strongly than pristine graphene, consistent with longer‐lived surface‐bound radicals that can couple. These findings help rationalize the widely used but poorly understood performance of reticulated vitreous carbon in organic electrosynthesis and offer guiding principles for rational carbon electrode design.

title: Non‐Fluorinated Electrolytes Enable Long‐Cycling Micron‐Sized Silicon Anodes
