abstract: ABSTRACT Microsized silicon (µm‐Si) anodes offer lower cost and higher tap density than their nanosized counterparts, however, their practical application remains challenging. A LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is widely considered essential for µm‐Si stable operation. However, potential environmental hazards of fluorides challenge the conventional use of lithium salts and additives for constructing LiF‐rich SEIs. Here, we present a non‐fluorinated electrolyte combining inorganic lithium salts (LiI/LiBr) with reduction‐resistant monoether solvents (tetrahydrofuran and hexyl methyl ether) forms a LiF‐free SEI that effectively addresses the rapid capacity fading of µm‐Si anodes. Unlike conventional mosaic‐structured SEI composed of oligomers and inorganic components (LiF and Li 2 O), our electrolyte forms high‐molecular‐weight polymers with binder‐like functionality at the silicon surface, preserving µm‐Si particle integrity and maintaining electrical connectivity even after pulverization. As a result, the µm‐Si electrode (D 50 = 4.65 µm) with an areal capacity of 3.15 mAh cm −2 achieves a Coulombic efficiency exceeding 99.95% and retains 92.12% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles at 0.3°C and 25°C. Furthermore, Li 3.75 Si||SPAN full cells achieve a capacity retention of over 79.43% after 150 cycles. This work provides an unconventional SEI design strategy for µm‐Si anodes.

title: Suppressing Ostwald Ripening Enables Programmable Growth of Radially Hierarchical MOF Superstructures Toward Multichannel Optical Waveguiding
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOF) homostructures or heterostructures with domain‐controlled emissive colors have demonstrated significant potential for high‐throughput sensing, anti‐counterfeiting, and information encryption. However, the precise construction of heterostructures with radially branched units remains challenging, primarily because the Ostwald ripening effect during crystal growth tends to drive one‐dimensional elongation. Here, we propose a programmable nucleation‐controlled strategy to spatially construct radially hierarchical MOF superstructures. During crystal growth, suppression of the Ostwald ripening effect triggers stable nucleation events in the system. Subsequently, the relatively high surface energy at the tips of 1D microrods promotes the secondary nucleation on the terminal facets, thereby leading to the formation of radially hierarchical superstructures. The acquired radial architectures with small angular deviations enable efficient multichannel optical signal output. The suppressing‐Ostwald‐ripening‐driven programmable growth paradigm provides a new route for the synthesis of multichannel waveguiding heterostructures and shows broad application prospects in advanced optoelectronic devices, multi‐channel information transmission, and encryption technologies.

title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

title: Defect and Ion-Migration Regulation in MAPbI3 Memristors via ZIF-67 Modification toward Stable Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-performance resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based on organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites remains limited by intrinsic vacancy defects and uncontrolled ion migration, which usually induce random conductive filaments (CFs) formation and poor device stability. Herein, a defect-engineering strategy is proposed by using a cobalt-based zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-67) as a multifunctional additive to synergistically regulate the MAPbI3 film through Co ion incorporation and ligand-assisted defect passivation. Structural, morphological, optical/electrical, and conduction analyses reveal that the introduction of ZIF-67 improves film quality by enlarging grains and reducing grain boundaries, while regulating Pb-vacancy-related defect states and introducing a stronger Co–I bond. These effects suppress disordered vacancy migration and promote stable CFs formation during resistive switching (RS). Consequently, the Cu/ZIF67-MAPbI3/p-Si device exhibits enhanced RS performance, including a high resistance ratio (>103), low operating power consumption (≈1.01 mW), endurance over 2300 cycles, and improved switching uniformity with reduced coefficients of variation for both high-resistance state and low-resistance state. Benefiting from its continuously tunable conductance, the device successfully emulates synaptic plasticity behaviors, including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD). Moreover, an experimentally calibrated multilayer perceptron achieves Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten digit recognition with an accuracy of 97.54% and a last loss of 3.35%, demonstrating the potential of ZIF67-MAPbI3-based RRAM device for artificial synapses and neuromorphic computing.

title: Tailoring Viscoelasticity by Carbon Filler Dimensionality toward High-Impact-Resistant Polydiborosiloxane Composites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of lightweight and flexible materials with high-impact-resistant performance remains a critical challenge under dynamic loading conditions, including precision instruments, electronics, and military defense systems. Herein, carbon fillers with distinct dimensionality are incorporated into polydiborosiloxane (PDBS) to construct composites with tunable viscoelastic behavior and excellent impact resistance. Increasing filler dimensionality not only retains the specific shear-stiffening viscoelastic behavior of PDBS but also significantly enhances the energy-dissipation capability and impact-resistant performance of the composites. Notably, the composite with large-size graphene achieves a high impact-force attenuation rate of 92.2% under low strain-rate impact while maintaining a strength of 48.8 MPa and a toughness of 24.2 MJ/m3 under high strain-rate impact. This work highlights the critical role of filler dimensionality in tailoring the viscoelasticity toward high-impact-resistant composite materials, thereby offering potential for efficient protection under dynamic loading conditions.

title: Preconstructed Electrolyte Interphase Enables Stable Commercial V2O5 Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) show great potential for large-scale energy storage on account of their exceptional safety, low cost, and environmental friendliness. As a representative cathode for AZIBs, commercial vanadium pentoxide (c-V2O5) still suffers from critical bottlenecks including severe vanadium dissolution, sluggish Zn2+ diffusion, and intensive interfacial side reactions in aqueous electrolytes. Herein, a novel electrochemical pretreatment strategy is developed to in-situ construct a uniform, compact ∼3 nm amorphous electrolyte interfacial layer (EIL) with an organic–inorganic composite structure on the surface of c-V2O5 in an organic lithium-ion battery system, which breaks through the limitations of unstable and inhomogeneous interfacial layers formed in conventional aqueous systems. The EIL exerts multifunctional effects by suppressing vanadium dissolution, accelerating ion diffusion, and inhibiting side reactions, endowing the modified electrode with a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.3%, outstanding cycling stability (180 mAh g–1 after 5000 cycles at a current density of 1 A g–1), and enhanced rate capability. This work could provide guidance for optimizing cathode materials of AZIBs through rational electrolyte interface engineering in the future.

title: Anharmonic Shear Vibration of Electrostatic Layers Leads to Low Thermal Conductivity in Bi2O2Se
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bi2O2Se is among the best n-type oxide thermoelectric materials with low lattice thermal conductivity and shows a robust ferroelectric state at room temperature in reduced dimensions. Herein, we have combined experimental and theoretical studies to comprehend this elusive congruence of low lattice thermal conductivity (κlat) and an incipient ferroelectric state. We have experimentally measured the κlat of Bi2O2Se in the 10–300 K temperature range, which showed that temperature–dependent κlat deviates from the usual T–1 dependence. Density functional theory-based calculation of phonon dispersion reveals that the low κlat in Bi2O2Se primarily originates from the anharmonic lattice vibration and the presence of low-frequency optical phonons, which strongly interact with the longitudinal acoustic phonons and suppress their dispersion along Γ-A and Γ-X directions in the Brillouin zone. Our study reveals that the lowest frequency optical phonons at ∼25.7 and ∼66.5 cm–1 involve a shear interlayer vibration that can promote distortion in the Bi–O bond length and displacement of Se atoms. We propose that these vibrational modes can dynamically break the centrosymmetric configuration in the reduced dimension, leading to the experimentally observed ferroelectricity in ultrathin nanosheets or flakes of Bi2O2Se as reported in the literature. We have corroborated the presence of these low-frequency phonons using low-temperature heat capacity measurement and temperature–dependent Raman spectroscopy.

title: RES NPs/GelMA Sustained-Release Cryogel Modulates Macrophage Arachidonic Acid Metabolism and Angiogenic Microenvironment Promoting Diabetic Wound Healing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Refractory chronic diabetic wounds severely impair quality of life. Their delayed healing is mainly driven by impaired angiogenesis and persistent inflammation caused by infection and excessive ROS. Resveratrol (RES) has anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Here, we developed a dual-mechanism sustained-release system for RES to promote diabetic wound healing. RES was converted into nanoparticles (RES NPs) to improve cellular uptake and bioavailability, then encapsulated in GelMA cryogel microspheres (CMS) for injectable, sustained release. This system downregulated NF-κB signaling, reduced ROS, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and COX2, thereby inhibiting arachidonic acid metabolism and promoting macrophage polarization from M1 to M2. Meanwhile, AMPK activation restored endothelial cell function, enhanced angiogenesis, and supported new vessel formation. Overall, this strategy accelerated high-quality wound repair in diabetic conditions.

title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young’s modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15–18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

title: Bubble-Guided Self-Healing Superhydrophobic Surfaces with Dual-Mode In Situ Visual Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Superhydrophobic surfaces exhibit great application potential ranging from sophisticated droplet manipulation to aerospace and other fields, owing to their unique properties such as liquid repellent, anti-corrosion, anti-icing, drag reduction, and so on. However, maintaining the stability of the solid–liquid interface remains a major challenge: the instability of the three-phase line caused by the collapse of the air layer during dynamic transport and the degradation of surface function caused by the retention of micro–nano contaminants seriously undermine its durability. In nature, rice leaves possess oriented microgroove architectures for unidirectional droplet transport, while submerged photosynthetic plants continuously generate bubbles to sustain intact solid–air–liquid (SAL) composite layers. Inspired by these merits, we propose a directional confinement–transport strategy, in which the microcolumn structure achieves dynamic compensation of the interfacial air layer through precise submillimeter bubble manipulation and establishes a cooperative stabilization of “structural confinement–air self-replenishment”. The surface demonstrates exceptional self-cleaning and no loss transport behaviors, vastly expanding its applicability in extreme environments. In addition, we construct a monitoring system based on interfacial chemical reactions, which enables in situ visual monitoring of the surface wetting state and can restore its superhydrophobicity on demand. In essence, this approach not only benefits the development of the superhydrophobic field, but also provides valuable theoretical foundations and practical guidance for constructing multifunctional stable interfaces, thereby propelling the field toward practical applications.

title: Synergistic Effects of Thermally Engineered Defect-Rich Structures in Renewable Nanocarbons for Enhanced Electrochemical Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical performance of conventional hard carbons remains constrained by their limited surface activity and insufficient interlayer spacing for efficient sodium storage. Here, we report a microstructurally engineered carbon derived from waste passenger tyres, exhibiting tunable defect density, interlayer spacing, and pore distribution through controlled carbonization between 700 and 1500 °C. The thermally driven reconstruction of sp2/sp3 domains induces a hierarchical framework featuring short-range ordered graphene nanodomains embedded within disordered carbon matrices, generating abundant closed and open pores that synergistically facilitate ion transport and adsorption. The optimized carbon produced at 1300 °C delivers a first-cycle reversible capacity of approximately 282.1 mAhg–1, retains approximately 278.5 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles at 10 mA g–1, and exhibits sustained high-current cycling stability over 500 cycles. Detailed micromechanistic analysis reveals that the enhanced sodium storage originates from the coupling of enlarged interlayer spacing (≈0.38–0.40 nm) and optimized Raman-active disorder with the internal pore architecture, enabling coexisting diffusion-controlled intercalation and surface-induced capacitive processes. This work establishes a framework for defect-controlled microstructural engineering of tyre-derived carbons, providing mechanistic insight into the pore–defect–graphite interplay and offering a sustainable pathway for converting end-of-life rubber waste into high-performance anode materials for next-generation sodium-ion batteries.

title: Biodegradable Starch/Gelatin/PAM Hydrogel Electrolyte for Wide-Temperature Flexible Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The booming development of flexible wearable electronics requires safe, deformable, and sustainable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Liquid electrolytes suffer leakage, zinc corrosion, and dendrite growth, while the recently reported hydrogel electrolytes fail to balance biodegradability and mechanical stretchability. Herein, we developed a fully biodegradable biomass dual-network hydrogel electrolyte fabricated via free-radical copolymerization of starch, gelatin, and acrylamide (AM) with ZnSO4 salts. Benefiting from abundant hydrogen-bond networks formed by renewable biomass skeletons, the tailored hydrogel effectively immobilizes free water to construct a water-poor interfacial microenvironment, simultaneously suppressing dendrite proliferation and electrolyte leakage. The hydrogel delivers an outstanding low-temperature tolerance and favorable ionic conductivity of 23.76 mS cm–1 (–20 °C) and contributes to accelerating redox reaction kinetics and improving the reversibility of the Zn plating/stripping process. Therefore, the assembled Zn||sodium vanadate battery delivers a high capacity of 350 mAh g–1 at 1.0 A g–1 with 100% Coulombic efficiency and 83% capacity retention over 700 cycles. Impressively, within a broad temperature window of 0–55 °C, the pouch cell could work under repeated bending states, and the hydrogel is fundamentally degraded within 20 days in natural soil. It provides a facile strategy for flexible and sustainable AZIBs with high performance.

title: Type-III Porous Liquid ZIF-8/Perfluorodecalin for O2 Delivery and CO2 Removal: Stability, Sorption, and Transport Monitored by In Situ EPR Spectroscopy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perfluorodecalin (C10F18) is a well-known gas carrier for chemical and biomedical applications. Being an inert and stable liquid, it is capable of dissolving and releasing large volumes of O2 and CO2. In this work, we propose a route for enhancing its functional properties furthermore by designing a type-III porous liquid (PL) composed of C10F18 and metal–organic framework ZIF-8. Using spin probes encapsulated in ZIF-8, we employ in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to investigate the stability of this PL and the adsorption, transport, and desorption of O2 and CO2 in practical conditions. The prototypical flow system with EPR detection was designed to demonstrate the controllable sorption cycles of ZIF-8/C10F18 PL. The exceptional stability and appealing functional properties of this PL pave the way for its future chemical and biomedical applications.

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Sleep declines in rural communities after electricity arrives
abstract: Scientists tracked the changing sleep patterns of Indigenous people in Argentina who gained access to mains electricity — and smart phones.

title: C–C Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic Reductants
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.

title: A DNA Origami Nanodevice Programs CD20 Spatial Organization for Selective Apoptosis of Malignant B Cells in Lymphoma Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triggering CD20 clustering to induce B cell apoptosis is considered a promising therapeutic strategy for dysregulated, B cell-driven diseases, yet current methods lack the spatial precision to organize CD20 into defined clusters and fail to discriminate malignant from normal B cells. Here, we describe an intelligent DNA origami nanodevice that integrates an optimized anti-CD20 antibody array with a conformational switch to selectively induce CD20 clustering and apoptosis in B-cell lymphoma. Benefiting from the nanometric precision of DNA origami, we found that arranging anti-CD20 antibodies into a pentavalent array with approximately 10 nm spacing most effectively drives CD20 clustering and downstream apoptosis. Under resting conditions, the nanodevice stays in a closed, tubular shape that conceals the antibody array inside and therefore remains harmless to normal B cells. Upon encountering c-Met expressed on lymphoma B cells, the device unrolls into a planar sheet and exposes the antibody array, triggering potent apoptotic signaling specifically in these malignant cells. In a Raji xenograft mouse model, intravenously injected nanodevices specifically unrolled at the tumor site, inhibited tumor growth by more than 70%, and produced no significant systemic toxicity. By coupling programmable ligand nanopatterning with a shape-changing switch, this DNA origami platform offers a generalizable strategy for receptor-mediated disease therapy.

title: Charge‐State‐Controlled Surface Modifiers for High‐Voltage and Stable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT For wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskites, quasi‐two‐dimensional (quasi‐2D) surface reconstruction using bulky‐cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium‐based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low‐dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic‐spacer charge‐state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs 0.2 FA 0.8 PbI 1.8 Br 1.2 wide‐bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N ‐methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge‐neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper‐like quasi‐2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap‐mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide‐ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO‐treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO‐treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS‐L‐1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge‐neutralized organic spacer for quasi‐2D surface reconstruction in wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.

title: In-memory phononic learning toward cognitive mechanical intelligence
abstract: Mechanical intelligence seeks autonomous materials that embody memory, perception, learning, and decision-making within the mechanical domain. A fundamental challenge is to integrate memory with information processing in an efficient, scalable, and interpretable way that supports cognitive learning and decision-making. Here, we introduce in-memory phononic learning, a framework that unifies non-volatile mechanical memory with wave-based perception in a phononic metastructure. Spatial information is stored as structural states that program elastic-wave responses, allowing probing waves to act as queries that retrieve informative features through parallel, physically transparent localization modes. Learning is achieved by offline optimization of input waveforms to selectively combine these features for multitask memory-pattern recognition without hardware redesign, with decisions inferred directly from output-energy responses. We experimentally and numerically demonstrate high-accuracy classification across tasks from geometric shapes to handwritten digits. Overall, this work elevates “materials that compute” toward “cognitive matter” that can interpret, reason, and learn through wave physics, laying a foundation for scalable and robust autonomous material systems.

title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
abstract:
All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10
                    4
                    at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
abstract:
Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away–mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys
                    526
                    (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo–electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C–DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
abstract:
Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of
                    Plasmodium
                    parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of
                    Plasmodium vivax
                    (
                    P. vivax
                    ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of
                    P. vivax
                    merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent
                    P. vivax
                    merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized
                    P. vivax
                    merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

title: Briefing Chat: How physicists successfully trapped the electron's antimatter equivalent
abstract: Nature staff discuss how precisely measuring a positron could shed light on one of physics’ greatest mysteries — plus, the latest on an ambitious mission to a Martian moon.

title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus
                    is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved
                    sasF
                    gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when
                    S. aureus
                    colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for
                    S. aureus
                    resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of
                    sasF
                    are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper
                    S. aureus
                    surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
abstract:
Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ
                    p
                     = 10.42 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    , μ
                    n
                     = 30.23 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml
                    −1
                    for
                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

title: Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO 2
abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide—a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits
abstract:
The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice,
                    Dmrt1
                    −/−
                    females are fertile, although they show a reduction of
                    Stra8
                    expression. Using our
                    DMRT1
                    mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation when
                    DMRT1
                    expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development,
                    DMRT1
                    −/−
                    gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.

title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N 2 O 5 hydrolysis
abstract:
Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
abstract:
Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in
                    Betula platyphylla
                    (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the
                    BpMYB123
                    promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator
                    BpMYB123
                    , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as
                    BpRD29B
                    . Disrupting
                    BpGAPDH
                    or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

title: Physical confinement modulates the rate-limiting transition in the release of phosphate from actin filaments
abstract:
The nucleotide state and rates of transitions between states regulate the dynamics of ATPases. Slow inorganic phosphate (P
                    i
                    ) release following ATP hydrolysis is often rate limiting and associated with key conformational changes. Actin filaments offer a unique opportunity to understand the fundamentals of P
                    i
                    release because identical subunits at filament ends and the interior release P
                    i
                    at markedly different rates. The molecular origin of this difference is debated, so we used extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize P
                    i
                    release from different subunits within an actin filament. The calculated dissociation rates of P
                    i
                    from ADP-Mg
                    2+
                    in the active site correlate with experimentally measured P
                    i
                    release rates and scale inversely with the numbers of water molecules in the cavity surrounding the γ-phosphate. Simulations show that egress of P
                    i
                    through the protein channels, including through the N111-R177 backdoor, is not rate limiting and that subunits at the filament ends use alternative egress pathways.

title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
abstract:
Enterococcus faecalis
                    is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How
                    E. faecalis
                    evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how
                    E. faecalis
                    biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that
                    E. faecalis
                    biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of
                    E. faecalis
                    , which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis
                    .
                    We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid–independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

title: Building digital pregnancies from the single cell up
abstract: Single-cell digital twins connect in vitro drug screening studies with clinical outcomes, providing a new framework to evaluate therapies and advance precision medicine in pregnancy.

title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
abstract:
Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4
                    +
                    T cells.

title: p75 NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
abstract:
The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75
                    NTR
                    ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis.
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75
                    NTR
                    axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    expression levels. Together, these data establish p75
                    NTR
                    as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75
                    NTR
                    axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength “island,” we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.

title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

title: Grain‐Boundary‐Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity‐Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity‐tolerant catalytic H 2 sensor based on a grain‐boundary‐rich palladium nanostructure (Pd GB ) that operates without any external heating. The Pd GB sensor functions reliably at 22°C–80°C and 0%–90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m −3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000‐fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H 2 ), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine‐learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H 2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature‐programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdH x formation for weakening H 2 O adsorption and suppress humidity‐induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials‐design strategy for next‐generation humidity‐tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

title: Harnessing Rare Earth Elements in Proteins and Functional Materials for Advanced Optical, Magnetic, and Mechanical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Rare earth‐proteins and their functional materials integrate unique physical properties of rare earth ions (RE 3+ ) with structural programmability of proteins, attracting increasing attention in a wide range of applications. Coordination with RE 3+ can enhance the rigidity and stability of certain proteins, even induce secondary structure transitions, and confer distinct physical properties onto functional materials. The programmability of amino acid sequences regulates coordination chemistry between proteins and RE 3+ , enabling the modulation of their optical and magnetic properties. Moreover, RE 3+ incorporation turns protein structures and aggregation state, leading to enhanced mechanical properties and adhesion strength. However, the development of such materials still faces significant challenges due to lack of molecular mechanism analysis and systematic rational design strategies. This review highlights the chemical structural analysis, rational design and synthesis strategies of rare earth‐protein and their functional materials. In addition, their applications in optics, magnetics, and mechanics are summarized. Finally, their current challenges and future perspectives are discussed.

title: Beyond State of Charge: Electrochemical States and Trajectory Design in Organic Mixed Conductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic redox, ion transport, solvation, structural reorganization, and mechanics, enabling diverse electrochemical functions but making their internal states poorly represented by scalar descriptors such as voltage, charge, conductivity, or nominal doping level. This Review establishes a state‐centered framework that treats electrochemical operation as the writing, observation, reconstruction, and design of multidimensional, history‐dependent state trajectories. A problem‐specific minimal sufficient state basis is introduced to distinguish essential from redundant coordinates, while waveform history and spatial heterogeneity define when lumped descriptions remain valid. Optical, electrical, ion‐specific, gravimetric, structural, mechanical, and temporal readouts are analyzed as selective projections whose complementarity determines state observability and hidden‐state reconstruction. Within this framework, congruence, kinetic ordering, decoupling, observational degeneracy, and mapping drift become experimentally testable relationships rather than isolated phenomena. Electrochromics, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), electrochemical memories, actuators, reconfigurable systems, and energy‐storage and conversion devices are then recast as technologies that select different trajectories through a shared electrochemical‐state landscape. The framework ultimately connects molecular structure, electrolyte, morphology, device architecture, and driving protocol to the inverse design of observable, controllable, reversible, and durable electrochemical trajectories.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Potential‐Driven Volcano Relationship in Grain Boundary Amorphicity and Ionic Transport of Antiperovskite Solid Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic transport in solid‐state electrolytes is governed by interfacial disorder and local chemical environments, yet their microscopic design principles remain challenging because large‐scale interfacial kinetics are simulated using molecular dynamics (MD), where predictive design requires quantum‐level accuracy. Here, we use an actively learned machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to bridge this scale‐accuracy gap in halide‐tunable antiperovskite solid electrolytes. By varying the local Cl − /Br − ratio and quantifying interfacial amorphicity and ion flux, we identify an MLIP‐driven volcano relationship between structural disorder and ionic transport. Cl‐enriched grain boundaries remain overly ordered, whereas Br − enrichment induces excessive disorder that disrupts migration. Intermediate halide compositions maximize ionic transport through moderately amorphous environments. Guided by this relationship, we design an anion‐engineered grain boundary through selective halide tuning. These results establish controlled anion segregation as a strategy for reducing interfacial resistance and highlight MLIP‐enhanced MD as a predictive framework for transport and disorder engineering in solid‐state materials.

title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah‐Level Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π–π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8‐tetraamino‐5,10‐dihydrophenazine‐1,4,6,9‐tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m 2 g −1 , delivers 242.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR‐FTIR and EQCM‐D measurements reveal that NH 4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH 4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H 3 O + for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe‐PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Moreover, the first Ah‐level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

title: A Novel pH‐Activatable Nanozyme for Treating Breast Cancer Bone Metastasis by Regulating Cancer Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and the Tumor Microenvironment
abstract: ABSTRACT Multi‐omics analyses implicate enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in breast cancer bone metastasis (BCBM). To target this metabolic vulnerability, we develop SPMMPA, a bone‐targeted nanozyme comprising a Prussian blue core, a disulfide‐bridged mesoporous silica interlayer, and a manganese oxide shell, functionalized with polyethylenimine, alendronate, and the Ser‐Asp‐Ser‐Ser‐Asp peptide. Its acid‐enhanced catalytic activity promotes reactive oxygen species production and glutathione depletion, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, reduced OXPHOS and adenosine triphosphate production, and downregulation of peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma coactivator 1‐alpha. Alendronate and silicon release contribute to reduced osteoclast activity and preservation of bone structure. Near‐infrared irradiation further enhances treatment efficacy through photothermal heating below 48°C. In mouse models of BCBM, SPMMPA suppresses tumor growth and alleviates osteolysis, without overt toxicity in the assays performed. These findings support a pH‐responsive catalytic strategy that couples disruption of tumor energy metabolism with protection of bone homeostasis.

title: Atomically Dispersed Fe–Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two‐Electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 Pathway for Reversible Li–CO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO 2 ) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO 2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li 2 C 2 O 4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 /ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li 2 C 2 O 4 . Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li 2 C 2 O 4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.

title: Operando Electro‐Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport‐Mechanical‐Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐ block ‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.

title: The Battery Data Commons registry
abstract: Public battery datasets are growing rapidly, but fragmented hosting and inconsistent descriptions make them difficult to find, compare, and reuse. Battery Data Commons presently indexes 349 datasets in a living, searchable metadata registry, using human- and machine-readable descriptions linked to the original sources. This exposes experimental context without relocating raw data to give datasets wider visibility and a second life to legacy ones. Together, these capabilities provide infrastructure for reproducible battery science, engineering, and AI-enabled innovation.

title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence–assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human–machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)–enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

title: Chemically encoded pH-tunable covalent adhesion by a bacterial thioester domain
abstract:
Thioester domains (TEDs) represent a family of bacterial adhesin domains that mediate covalent anchoring to target ligands via an intramolecular thioester bond. Although the broad distribution of TEDs among Gram-positive bacteria suggests a critical functional role, the biological significance of this covalent mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that TED-mediated covalent anchoring is reversible and that its equilibrium is regulated by pH. Specifically, SfbI-TED from group A
                    Streptococcus
                    binds tightly to fibrinogen at physiological pH, whereas mild acidification to pH 6.0 induces rapid dissociation of the complex. Thermodynamic analyses indicated that this pH responsiveness is largely dictated by the intrinsic pH sensitivity of the thioester-mediated acyl transfer reaction conserved within TEDs, rather than by surface residues specific to individual TEDs. Similar pH-dependent behavior was observed in phylogenetically distinct TEDs, suggesting that pH-responsive adhesion is likely to be a broadly shared feature of TED-containing adhesins across Gram-positive bacteria.

title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe 2
abstract:
Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe
                    2
                    /LiAl
                    2
                    Fe
                    3
                    O
                    8
                    (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe
                    2
                    /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe
                    2
                    .
