The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe
                    2
                    . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
abstract:
Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients:

Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional–printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4 + T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4
                    +
                    responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4
                    +
                    response was strongly T helper 1 (T
                    H
                    1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T
                    H
                    2 cytokines. Both CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
abstract:
Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3:

Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

abstract:

Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi–one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.

title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
abstract:
The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning–based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector
                    Anopheles coluzzii
                    in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the
                    orco
                    and
                    IR76b
                    chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between
                    An. coluzzii
                    and
                    Aedes aegypti
                    linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
abstract:
Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10
                    7
                     per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10
                    8
                     per milliliter in soils, and 10
                    9
                     per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

title: CREBBP loss drives immune evasion by epigenetically silencing STING and MHC-I in small cell lung cancer
abstract:
Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify
                    CREBBP
                    loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in
                    Rb1/Trp53
                    -driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently,
                    Crebbp
                    deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically,
                    Crebbp
                    loss suppresses
                    Sting
                    and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both
                    Crebbp
                    -mutant and
                    Crebbp
                    -wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in
                    Crebbp
                    -mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish
                    CREBBP

title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

title: Unveiling the role of crystallinity of RuO2 catalysts for regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction
abstract: The intrinsic role of crystallinity in regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on RuO2 remains elusive due to the synthetic challenge of decoupling structural order from compositional variations. Here, we develop an oxygen-partial-pressure-controlled pyrolysis strategy to achieve graded crystallinity in pure RuO2 nanocatalysts, establishing a pristine model to elucidate this structure-function relationship. We reveal that amorphous RuO2 features disordered dangling oxygen that readily undergoes protonation, triggering a rapid but degradative lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM) with an ultralow overpotential of 154 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Conversely, increasing crystallinity stabilizes the RuO6 framework, suppressing protonation and shifting the pathway toward the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM). Crucially, highly crystalline RuO2 demands excessive cell voltages (1.72 V at 1.0 A cm−2) in proton exchange membrane electrolyzers, paradoxically accelerating oxidative etching. This work uncovers a crystallinity-driven LOM-to-AEM transition, identifying intermediate crystallinity as a practical strategy for balancing activity and stability.

title: Two pathways driving Phanerozoic temperature change: low-latitude radiative forcing and outgassing-weathering-vegetation carbon feedbacks
abstract: Two potentially interacting pathways may have shaped Phanerozoic temperature change: radiative effects linked to low-latitude land area and carbon-cycle feedbacks involving volcanic outgassing, silicate weathering, and terrestrial organic-carbon burial. title: Electrons and phonons running hot and cold in boron arsenide
A Full-Duplex Metasurface for Simultaneous and Independent Control of Radiation and Reflection
abstract: Metasurfaces have transformed electromagnetic interfaces from fixed, material-defined boundaries into engineered platforms for tailoring wave propagation, spanning both passive designs and actively programmable implementations. For future information systems, a central challenge is to make the same physical aperture operate simultaneously as a radiating antenna and a reconfigurable reflector. Radiation–reflection-integrated (R2I) metasurfaces combine these functions, but their responses remain coupled: configuring the surface for radiation constrains its behavior in reflection. They therefore cannot generally provide independent operation at the same time, frequency, and polarization. Here, we show an intelligent full-duplex R2I metasurface that overcomes this constraint. The surface integrates controllable meta-atoms with a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW). Because the SIW-guided and free-space excitations occupy largely separated regions of the spatial spectrum, the radiated and reflected fields can be manipulated simultaneously and independently on the same aperture. We experimentally demonstrate this capability in integrated sensing and communication and in integrated detection and stealth, both realized using a single artificial-intelligence-assisted metasurface under identical operating conditions. These results establish a route towards full-duplex, single-aperture information systems.

title: Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide Liquid Crystals with Enhanced Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anisotropic NMR spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of complex small molecules. Compared with residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), however, the application of residual chemical shift anisotropies (RCSAs) has remained relatively limited, largely owing to the lack of simple and efficient methods for their acquisition. Here, we report a biphasic polyarylisocyanide lyotropic liquid-crystalline (LLC) system based on single-handed helical polyisocyanides prepared by alkyne-Pd(II)-catalyzed controlled polymerization. The biphasic nature of this medium enables straightforward extraction of ΔRCSAs from a single one-dimensional 13C NMR experiment on a single sample, without requiring specialized instrumentation, devices, or postcorrection. We demonstrate the broad applicability of this approach by measuring ΔRCSAs for eight structurally diverse natural products and organic molecules. The resulting 13C ΔRCSAs are sufficiently large to enable reliable structural verification and stereochemical elucidation. Notably, the method allowed us to unambiguously resolve previously questionable 13C NMR assignments in cryptotanshinone. In addition, the chiral LLC medium exhibits pronounced enantiodiscrimination, as demonstrated for indanol enantiomers as well as significant enantiodifferentiating capabilities for several natural alkaloids. Furthermore, 19F RCSA measurements enable direct differentiation of two enantiomers even within a racemic mixture. Together, these results establish biphasic polyarylisocyanide LLCs as a simple, robust, and broadly applicable alignment platform for ΔRCSA measurements, thereby expanding the utility of anisotropic NMR for structural elucidation and chiral molecular characterization.

title: Photoinduced Ge(II)-Catalyzed Divergent Functionalization of Pyridyl Halides via Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes

abstract: Abstract We report a photoinduced Ge(II)-catalyzed strategy for divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides that leverages in situ electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex formation to catalytically generate pyridyl radicals, enabling aryl, alkynyl, and alkenyl couplings under mild, protic conditions without an external photocatalyst. Notably, the protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity for pyridyl C–X bonds, leaving other aryl halides, including those bearing electron-withdrawing substituents, intact. The protocol further enables unique transformations, including complete C8-selective coupling with 7-aminoquinoline and the modular assembly of benzo[f]isoquinolines from alkenyl boron reagents. Mechanistic studies support an EDA-mediated radical pathway. This work provides a sustainable platform for the divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides and expands the application of main-group elements in catalytic EDA chemistry.

title: Low-Temperature Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics into Metal–Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The selective semihydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes is an important industrial process for the production of bulk and fine chemicals. However, the activity and selectivity trade-off of alkyne hydrogenation has been a long-standing challenge, due to undesirable overhydrogenation or insufficient activity of the designed catalysts. Here, we report a sustainable route for high-performance alkyne hydrogenation using a metal–organic framework (MOF) confined PdNi cluster (PdcNi) catalyst, synthesized directly from waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics under low-temperature aqueous conditions. The PdcNi@UiO-66 catalyst with dispersed Pd clusters anchored on Ni clusters not only maximizes Pd utilization but also establishes a new pathway for the recycling of plastics. Importantly, when employed as a catalyst for phenylacetylene semihydrogenation, PdcNi@UiO-66 exhibited outstanding activity and selectivity, achieving a turnover frequency (TOF) of up to 67,470 h–1 at 65 °C. This performance significantly surpasses that of previously reported catalysts and is nearly 20 times higher than that of the commercial Lindlar catalyst. DFT calculations combined with experimental results reveal that the PdcNi cluster exhibits a moderate adsorption strength toward both reactants and target products, compared with its nanoparticle and single-atom counterparts. This balanced adsorption leads to a more favorable thermodynamic tendency for styrene desorption rather than overhydrogenation, ultimately contributing to the high activity and selectivity. This study demonstrates a direct route to transforming PET waste into high-performance MOF-based catalysts for selective hydrogenation, offering a cost-effective and sustainable solution for plastic recycling and the development of high-performance catalysts.

title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Isomerization Strategy Enables Balanced Energy Dissipation of NIR-II AIEgens for “One-for-All” Tumor Phototheranostics
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract “One-for-all” phototheranostics with the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emission have garnered great enthusiasm for seamlessly integrating superb imaging and high-efficiency therapy into a single formula. However, it is still a nontrivial conundrum to achieve balanced excited-state energy dissipation to guarantee high NIR-II brightness, photothermal conversion, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. As a powerful tool for balancing radiative and nonradiative decays, aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) are emerging as a promising frontier in developing “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents, while their phototheranostic performance needs to be further improved. In this contribution, we designed and synthesized two positional isomers, 5BT-PBPT and 6BT-PBPT, by attaching donors at the 5- and 6-positions of the benzo[b]thiophene (BT) segment, respectively, to investigate the effect of positional isomerism on the phototheranostic performance of NIR-II AIEgens. Interestingly, both experimental and computational results demonstrate that the isomerization affords great strength in tuning energy levels, structural conformations, aggregation behaviors, and excited-state energy dissipation. Consequently, a sweet spot for fully utilizing excitation energy was achieved in 5BT-PBPT nanoparticles (NPs), which exhibited not only strong NIR absorption but also high NIR-II fluorescence brightness, strong ROS production, and excellent photothermal conversion efficiency (η). Benefiting from this, 5BT-PBPT NPs afforded superior performance in the “one-for-all” phototheranostics for orthotopic breast tumor treatment. This study fully demonstrates the effectiveness of the isomeric engineering strategy in comprehensively improving the phototheranostic capabilities of NIR-II AIEgens and thereby provides an effective approach for the construction of high-performance NIR-II “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents.

title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.

title: Solid–Liquid Transitions in 1D Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A lack of melt processability is noted for emerging hybrid material systems like metal–organic frameworks, lead-halide perovskites, and metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas). Here, we report reversible solid-to-liquid phase transitions ranging from 67 to 184 °C in silver secondary-alkanethiolate 1-dimensional (1D) MOChas. These MOChas were synthesized using five different secondary alkanethiols: 2-propanethiol, 2-butanethiol, 2-pentanethiol, 3-hexanethiol, and 4-heptanethiol. Structural characterization using small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography (smSFX) reveals a 1D wire crystal motif. These 1D wire lattices exhibit green-yellow photoluminescence that disappears upon melting. The low melting temperature is attributed to the conformational flexibility of the secondary alkanethiol ligands, providing entropic benefits for the amorphous state. Furthermore, the transition from a nonmolecular, infinite covalent (Ag-SR)∞ network in the solid state to oligomolecular species (Ag-SR)x in the molten state contributes to a higher enthalpy of fusion. Large crystallites are observed to evolve from the liquid near the phase transition temperature. Notably, unmixing of chiral domains occurs in the racemic crystals while the inorganic network remains unchanged.

title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model
abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

title: Breaking Symmetry Cancellation: Heterovalent Substitution Unlocks Ultrastrong, Phase-Matchable Nonlinearity in Deep-Ultraviolet Tetrahedral Crystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Deep-ultraviolet (deep-UV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals demand a challenging integration of strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), sufficient birefringence for phase matching (PM), and a wide bandgap (λ < 200 nm). In tetrahedron-based materials, the hyperpolarizabilities of constituent tetrahedra usually nearly cancel due to structural symmetry, resulting in weak SHG and small birefringence─a classic example being α-SiO2. Breaking this symmetry-driven cancellation while retaining deep-UV transparency thus represents a key chemical design challenge. Here, we report a deep-UV transparent NLO crystal BeSO4 derived from α-SiO2 via stepwise heterovalent tetrahedral substitution. This crystal crystallizes in the noncentrosymmetric tetragonal space group, with alternating BeO4 and SO4 tetrahedra forming [Be3S3O18] six-membered rings. By effectively breaking the symmetry cancellation via alternating low-valence (Be2+) and high-valence (S6+) tetrahedra, BeSO4 achieves a deep-UV cutoff at 176 nm, an exceptional SHG response of 5.1 × KDP at 1064 nm─the strongest among all deep-UV sulfates and Be-containing deep-UV crystals, and a birefringence of 0.038 at 590 nm, almost seven times that of the isostructural BPO4. Unlike BPO4 and α-SiO2, BeSO4 exhibits SHG behavior consistent with phase-matchability, and under 532 nm excitation, it produces a detectable second-harmonic signal at 266 nm. First-principles calculations reveal that the enhanced performance originates from shorter S–O bonds, stronger orbital hybridization, a narrower bandgap, and highly anisotropic electron density, all stemming from the successful cancellation-breaking strategy. It should be noted that the main novelty of this work lies in single-crystal growth, linear/nonlinear optical properties, and mechanistic analysis, since the crystal structure of BeSO4 has been previously reported.

title: Solid-State NMR Reveals a Bifunctional Disordered Linker That Couples Katanin Microtubule Anchoring to Condensate-Activated Severing
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Microtubule severing by katanin drives rapid cytoskeletal remodeling for cell fate decision, yet how the catalytic subunit p60 (Kp60) recognizes the microtubule lattice to achieve efficient severing remains unresolved. Here, we report that the N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of Kp60 is an essential bifunctional module for severing activity. Using solid-state NMR (ssNMR), we identified a microtubule-binding domain (MTBD) within the IDR which directly engages the lattice to guide substrate anchoring. Surprisingly, the same IDR also enables Kp60 phase separation. Our ssNMR analyses of the condensed phase pinpointed three discrete interaction regions within the IDR which cooperatively orchestrate this multivalent assembly. Importantly, Kp60 phase separation was associated with markedly increased ATPase activity, supporting a functional link between condensation and enzymatic activation. Using function-separation-mutation analyses, our studies show both microtubule binding and condensation are essential for severing: microtubule targeting provides spatial specificity, while condensation provides the catalytic threshold through local enrichment. Thus, the Kp60 IDR constitutes a bifunctional interface that integrates substrate recognition with enzymatic robustness, thereby establishing phase separation as a fundamental and efficient regulator of microtubule dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling.

title: Operando Time-Resolved Spectroelectrochemical Microscopy Reveals Distinct Electron Depletion Pathways in Electrocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding electrocatalysis requires direct knowledge of how charge carriers are distributed and consumed at active sites under the operating conditions. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of injected electrons in working catalysts remain largely inaccessible, hindering a mechanistic understanding of catalytic heterogeneity. Here, we develop an operando time-resolved spectroelectrochemical microscopy that enables direct and quantitative mapping of electron density with microsecond temporal resolution and micrometer spatial resolution. Using monolayer MoS2 as a model system, we directly visualize the spatial redistribution and depletion of electrochemically injected electrons during the hydrogen evolution reaction. We observe pronounced site-specific electron depletion that correlates with catalytic activity and further identify two distinct mechanisms governing charge loss: reaction-limited depletion at highly active sites, including edges and Pt-functionalized sites, and injection-limited depletion in bilayer regions. These results establish a quantitative link between local charge carrier dynamics and catalytic activity and provide a general framework for probing nanoscale carrier dynamics in electrocatalysts.

title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

title: Hybrid Solid Oxide Cell Enables Efficient and Robust High-Temperature CO2 Electrolysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route toward a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but balancing mechanical robustness and electrochemical performance remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge by introducing a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that spatially decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport, and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell combines high mechanical robustness (fracture load > 7 N) with 1.5–3.0-fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over 600–800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm2, achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes an effective strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.

title: Unraveling Water Balances behind Salt Formation in CO2 Reduction Electrolyzers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Salt precipitation in CO2 electrolyzers remains a critical barrier to long-term stability, yet the underlying water-salt transport and balance are poorly understood. Here, we established a quantitative mass balance framework to account for water entering and leaving the cathode chamber from all possible sources and across different phases, thereby elucidating the origin of bicarbonate salt formation. We revealed that although the inlet CO2 stream typically flows through a water bubbler, it is often not fully saturated with water vapor and thus results in significant liquid water evaporation inside the cathode chamber. Although water crossover from the anolyte to the cathode is, in principle, sufficient to dissolve the cotransported K+ as carbonate species (or even bicarbonate in some cases), evaporation reduces the effective local liquid water-to-K+ ratio, leading to salt precipitation. Conversely, excessive humidification suppresses salt formation but induces electrode wetting and flooding, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between dehydration-induced crystallization and overhumidification-driven mass transport limitations. Together, these findings establish water management as a governing principle for stabilizing CO2 electrolyzers and provide engineering guidelines for controlling salt formation in electrochemical reactor systems.

title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

title: Hot Carrier Cooling Dynamics in Tin Tri-Iodide Perovskites Thin Films
abstract: Abstract Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.

title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH 2 OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. Metallic bismuth (Bi) is intrinsically active for this reaction, yet undergoes severe structural degradation under continuous electrolysis—a failure mode we identify as electrochemical spongification, wherein the compact Bi framework cathodically relaxes into an electrically disconnected porous network. Herein, we report an “asymmetric electrochemical breathing” strategy that effectively decouples long‐term catalytic durability from structural failure. Using pulsed potentials between −1.36 and +1.24 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl nanosheets serve as a dynamic template, delivering a high Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% and a yield rate of 4.29 mmol h −1 cm −2 , among the highest reported for NH 2 OH electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical insights reveal that BiOCl rapidly reduces in situ to dense metallic Bi to drive efficient nitrate reduction. Crucially, a brief anodic pulse reconstructs the framework before irreversible degradation occurs, enabling continuous structural rejuvenation for over 380 h. This dynamic reconstruction strategy successfully suppresses the Faradaic efficiency decay rate by two orders of magnitude, establishing a robust paradigm for stabilizing highly active yet metastable electrocatalysts.

title: Electrosynthesis of p ‐Hydroxybenzoic Acid From Phenol and CO 2
abstract: ABSTRACT P ‐hydroxybenzoic acid ( p ‐HBA), with wide applications in food preservatives, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystalline polyether, is currently synthesized via the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction using anhydrous phenolate (PhO − ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). However, this reaction typically suffers from poor selectivity, and requires high temperature/pressure, strongly base, and metal/organic cations for selectivity control. Herein, we report a new method for the electrosynthesis of p ‐HBA from phenol (PhOH) and CO 2 by iodine mediation, achieving 61% yield and 90% selectivity without strong bases and metal cations under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Mechanism studies indicated that PhOH was first selectively iodinated by iodine cations (I + ) generated at the anode to form p ‐iodophenol (HOPh‐I). Subsequently, HOPh‐I and CO 2 were respectively activated on Ag catalyst with abundant grain boundaries (GB‐Ag) through single‐electron reduction, and then underwent radical coupling processes to produce p ‐HBA. Notably, this electrochemical method also successfully converted various oxygen‐containing and nitrogen‐containing aromatic compounds, including the typical structural units of lignin and its derivatives, into valuable carboxylic acids. This innovative electrochemical approach overcomes the inherent limitations of the traditional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, offering a promising strategy for the sustainable utilization of CO 2 and biomass resources.

title: Breaking the π‐Conjugation‐Dependence: Enhanced Birefringence and SHG Response in Densely Packed Deep‐UV Phosphates
abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing birefringence and SHG in deep‐UV NLO crystals based on tetrahedral oxyanions remains challenging as extending π‐conjugation often sacrifices UV transparency. In this study, we propose a synergic design strategy that correlates π‐conjugation degree, packing density, and optical performance, resulting in two formamidinium phosphate crystals, enabling two deep‐UV NLO crystals, [CH(NH 2 ) 2 ]H 2 PO 4 ( I ) and [CH(NH 2 ) 2 ] 2 HPO 4 ( II ), with simultaneously enhanced birefringence (0.10@550 nm of I and 0.15@550 nm of II ) and SHG responses (1.1 × KDP of I and 2.0 × KDP of II ). Notably, birefringence of compound II outperforms a number of guanidinium‐based and phosphate‐based NLO crystals, endowing it with exceptional comprehensive performance, as evidenced by its highest quality factor ( Q = 4.4 for II) . Due to the superior birefringence and SHG intensity, both I and II realize phase‐matching at fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm and 532 nm. Structure–property relationship studies reveal that formamidinium's small steric size facilitates dense packing of building blocks within lattice, thereby enhancing birefringence and SHG. This work elucidates the critical influence of π‐conjugation degree on packing density and overall performance (SHG intensity and birefringence). Based on these findings, a novel design pathway for deep‐UV materials might be proposed, linking π‐conjugation degree and packing density with SHG and birefringence.

title: Ni 3 (HITP) 2 @PTFE Molecular Fence Enables Selective C 2 Coupling in Methane Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis (CEC) enables methane activation under ambient conditions; however, the poorly understood interfacial active sites and uncontrolled evolution of reactive radical intermediates cause methane conversion to remain dominated by C 1 oxygenation rather than selective C─C coupling. Herein, we assemble the established Ni 3 (HITP) 2 framework (HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) on PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) to construct a molecular fence interface integrating Ni–N 4 sites with spatial confinement for selective C 2 coupling. During CEC, contact electrification at the PTFE–water interface supports radical generation for methane conversion, while the coupled Ni–N 4 sites further facilitate O 2 activation and modulate reactive species utilization. Simultaneously, the porous Ni 3 (HITP) 2 outer layer shows enhanced CH 4 uptake near the charged interface and is proposed to favor C─C coupling by promoting local methane enrichment and retention of methane‐derived intermediates. As a result, methane conversion is redirected from C 1 oxygenation toward selective C 2 coupling under ambient conditions, delivering a C 2 yield of 0.58 mmol g −1 h −1 with 82.4% selectivity. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations support a mechanistic model in which interfacial Ni–N 4 sites and the porous framework jointly influence reactive‐species utilization and methane‐derived intermediate reactions, favoring pathway‐selective methane CEC.

title: Biomimetic Molybdenum Chemistry Spanning all Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families: From Stoichiometric Oxygen Atom Transfer to Catalytic C─H Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C─H hydroxylation, through Mo VI /Mo IV cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolene‐coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have struggled to replicate this versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive Mo V dimers, and catalytic turnover remains scarce. Here we report that a [N 2 S 2 ] 2− ‐supported Mo IV ═O complex abstracts oxygen atoms from substrates representative of three molybdopterin enzyme families: Me 2 SO, Me 3 NO, ClO 4 − , NO 3 − , and SeO 4 2− (DMSO reductases); methionine sulfoxide (sulfite oxidases); and benzamidoxime and N ‐hydroxyphthalimide (mARCs). In the cases of ClO 4 − and NO 3 − , oxygen atom transfer (OAT) requires Lewis acid activation by B(C 6 F 5 ) 3 . The corresponding Mo VI (O) 2 redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, akin to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C─H hydroxylation of substrates inspired by the XO family, thus demonstrating reactivity that spans all four molybdopterin families. Coupling OAT and hydride transfer half‐reactions enables catalytic turnover, as demonstrated here for both benzimidazoline C─H hydroxylation and formate decarboxylation using DMSO as terminal oxidant, thus demonstrating the first examples of catalytic C─H oxidation by a molybdopterin‐inspired synthetic platform.

title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.

title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF achieves up to 99% H 2 O 2 selectivity and a flow‐cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow‐Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic in‐sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co‐localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation–anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion‐migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo‐modulation is further attenuated by exciton–polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion‐migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3‐(1‐vinyl‐3‐imidazolyl)‐propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro‐ and photo‐synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation–anion pair prevents long‐distance ion‐migration, ensuring strong cation–anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi‐wavelength photo‐synaptic modulation coupled with electro‐synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application‐relevant in‐sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color‐guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian‐speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing‐computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.

title: Engineered Excited‐State Coupling Enables Efficient Exciton Harvesting in Binuclear Copper Iodide Cluster Scintillators
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low‐cost, high‐performance x‐ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu–I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin‐orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x‐ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation‐induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation‐state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu–I clusters with nearly identical x‐ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited‐state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water‐resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV −1 and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm −1 . Furthermore, tandem integration with a high‐Z scintillator enables selective density‐discriminating x‐ray imaging and micro‐computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high‐throughput development of promising metal‐cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.

title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs 4 PbBr 6 and CsPbBr 3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high‐performance perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next‐generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs 4 PbBr 6 phase often accompanies CsPbBr 3 crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive‐mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3‐carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3‐CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr 3 formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs 4 PbBr 6 and CsPbBr 3 phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr 3 phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs 4 PbBr 6 phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.

title: Electronic Coupling and Dual‐Spillover Effect in Co/Co 7 Fe 3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Rational design of dual‐site catalysts to decouple complex multi‐electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co 7 Fe 3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO 3 RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4‐electron step reduces NO 3 − to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4‐electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4‐electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well‐defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co 7 Fe 3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO 3 RR through synergistic dual‐spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near‐unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH 3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h −1 cm −2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn‐nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm −2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.

title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N 4 . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N 4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O 2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

title: Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress‐ROS‐Inflammation Cycle With Antibacterial Heterojunctions for Periodontitis Therapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT In periodontitis, recalcitrant biofilms and the vicious endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle cause persistent inflammatory osteolysis. However, current treatments mainly alleviate infection and inflammation, without targeting this ER stress‐centered etiological circuit. Herein, we report the de novo design of an ER‐regulating heterojunction (ERR‐HJ), composed of cobalt selenide (CoSe), Ti 3 C 2 MXene, and taurine, for periodontitis treatment via bacterial clearance, ER homeostasis maintenance, and alveolar bone regeneration. Our studies demonstrate that the unique structure of the CoSe/Ti 3 C 2 heterojunction can scavenge ROS and easily transfer electrons from H 2 O 2 to bacterial membranes, which disrupts bacterial respiration and metabolism. At the cellular level, the heterojunction with taurine activates selenoprotein metabolism, restores redox balance, and alleviates ER stress by dampening the PERK‐CHOP pathway, collectively reprogramming macrophages towards a tissue‐regenerative M2 phenotype while inhibiting their osteoclastogenic differentiation. Strikingly, the osteogenic differentiation of human periodontal ligament cells is profoundly boosted. In periodontitis models, the ERR‐HJ promotes tissue repair and reduces alveolar bone resorption through concomitant suppression of oxidative stress, ER stress, and inflammation, suggesting the disruption of the self‐perpetuating cycle. This work furnishes an intriguing avenue for developing innovative heterojunction biomaterials to treat bacterial infection‐associated disorders by integrating bacterial killing and ER stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle inhibition.

title: Capillary physics links HIV capsid geometry to nuclear pore translocation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The protective capsid encasing the genetic material of HIV can traverse the nuclear pore complex (NPC) intact, despite being far larger than conventional passive cargo. This is attributed to the properties of the capsid surface, which promote partitioning into cohesive assemblies of the disordered proteins that form the NPC’s permeability barrier: phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG-Nups). The implication, at the mesoscale, is that capsid–NPC interactions are characterized by the interfacial physics of wetting and capillarity. To capture this, we develop a minimal theory that reduces to an interplay between capsid geometry, effective cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic contact angles, and a ratio of interfacial tensions. By combining analytical calculations, sharp- and diffuse-interface numerics, we make several predictions: A geometry-dependent trade-off between penetration depth and the wetting transition; asymmetric capillary forces that generate torques and lead to metastable “stalled” states that are tilted; a topological classification of the possible mechanisms underlying the largest energetic barrier; and spontaneous symmetry breaking of displaced FG-Nups. These behaviors connect capsid shape and orientation to the topology and symmetry of FG-Nup displacement, and to the molecular compositions on each side of the pore. They are consistent with published cryoelectron tomography orientations, which provide an initial estimate of the cytoplasmic contact angle. Crucially, our results identify a capillary advantage for the HIV capsid’s characteristic broken-symmetry geometry.

title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is constrained by rapid RNA degradation during sample storage, necessitating cold-chain logistics. Here we present spatially confined biosilicification (SCB), wherein RNA is encapsulated within a nanoscopic layer of amorphous silicon dioxide, as a highly effective methodology enabling ambient-temperature preservation of single-cell transcriptomes. By judiciously incorporating a silicification inhibitor, SCB achieves spatiotemporal control over both intra- and extracellular silica deposition, preventing excessive crosslinking and cell aggregation while preserving RNA biointegrity and accessibility. scRNA-seq performed with biosilicified cells (Si-scRNA-seq) maintained high transcriptomic fidelity with fresh samples (R
                    2
                    = 0.95 after 7 d) extending RNA half-life to 54.8 d at 25 °C, a 685-fold improvement compared to unprotected samples. Furthermore, Si-scRNA-seq confers robust resistance against oxidative and UV degradation. Compatible with mainstream platforms at ~0.1 RMB per sample, Si-scRNA-seq successfully resolves cellular heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver, and ovarian cancer specimens after extended room-temperature storage. Si-scRNA-seq provides a scalable and cold-chain–free solution for single-cell transcriptomics in research and clinical settings.

title: Integrating ecology with genetics to explain gene reuse during repeated evolution
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The role of determinism and chance in the evolutionary history of life is often analyzed through the lens of the repeatability of evolution. Although it is now clear that evolution often repeats itself, we are only beginning to understand why this varies in degree. For example, the probability of gene reuse during repeated bouts of adaptation often declines with time since divergence, but the causes of this pattern remain unclear. Here, we explore two core hypotheses for time-dependent variation in the repeatability of gene reuse during adaptation. Specifically, gene reuse depends on the extent to which lineages have 1) similar genomes such that they have similar genetic architectures, mutations, and mutational effects (i.e., a fairly well-appreciated “shared genetics” hypothesis), and 2) similar ecologies such that they have similar environments and patterns of natural selection (i.e., a mostly unexplored “shared ecology” hypothesis). The latter hypothesis emphasizes ecology’s role in gene reuse and has received little explicit attention. In particular, testing the shared ecology hypothesis requires moving beyond a simple dichotomous characterization of ecology to embracing ecological divergence as a multivariate and continuous phenomenon. Although such tests are only beginning to emerge, they already illustrate how integration of ecological factors can help explain variation in gene reuse. Here, we advocate a framework that integrates the influence of both genetic and ecological factors in the repeatability of evolution and can be applied to a range of organisms to better understand the role of determinism and chance in biological diversification.
